intro.text: **Built for live conversations.** Pick who you're talking to, then go to **🗡️ Offense** (you bring the case) or **🛡️ Defense** (they raised an objection).
Doctrinal frame: our church's Articles of Faith. One Being, three Persons; Christ has two natures; Scripture alone.

Pray first. Only the Spirit opens eyes (John 6:44; 2 Cor 4:4–6). Watch your own heart for pride; the goal is their soul, not the point (2 Tim 2:24–26). What helps in real conversations isn't knowing more verses. It's **how you run the conversation**. Use these moves every time.

moves.title: Phase 1 = agree on the plain text. Nothing else moves until they do.
moves.text: Read the verse and ask a yes/no question about what it *says* (not what it means). Don't go on until they answer. *"I'm not moving to Phase 2 until you answer Phase 1."*

moves.title: Yes/no questions, one at a time.
moves.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"* Short questions are hard to wriggle out of. Long statements give them room to filibuster.

moves.title: Call out the dodge out loud.
moves.text: When they redefine a word ("personification," "communicates information," "a vibe"), name it: *"I didn't ask about personification. I asked, can He speak?"*

moves.title: Use their rule on another verse.
moves.text: When they invent a rule for one verse (e.g. "no article = 'a god'"), apply the same rule somewhere it obviously fails (John 1:6 becomes "a man sent from *a god* named *a John*").

moves.title: Hold them to their own analogy.
moves.text: If they bring an analogy (king and messenger, software coder, three judges), don't swap it out. Push it until it proves your point: *"Can the agent of the king claim to BE the king?"*

moves.title: No topic-hopping.
moves.text: When a point lands, people often jump to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity makes no sense." Don't follow. *"Let's finish this one first, then I'm happy to go there."*

moves.title: Name the goalpost shift.
moves.text: *"First you wanted a Bible verse. I gave you the verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' own mouth?"*

moves.title: "What's the only thing we do? Read."
moves.text: When they say "context," make *them* show the verse in the context. Then wait. Silence works for you.

moves.title: Ask the question back.
moves.text: End with a question they have to answer on their own (*"Who is the Father hearing from?"*), not a speech.

moves.title: Stay warm.
moves.text: Even when they get angry or walk away: *"I want you to be saved, brother. I love you."* Truth with love keeps the door open (1 Pet 3:15–16).

universalTools.title: "Yahweh" isn't one-person-only.
universalTools.text: Yahweh is the name of the one true God, and Scripture applies it to the Father, the Son and the Spirit. Their "then Jesus is his own Father" syllogism only works if Yahweh = the Father alone. A name can have more than one referent: "Judah" can mean a man *or* a tribe (Judges 1:1–2).

universalTools.title: Word–concept fallacy.
universalTools.text: "'Trinity' isn't in the Bible" → neither are "monotheism" or "Bible." The question is whether the *concept* is there.

universalTools.title: Three in one way, one in another.
universalTools.text: Not a contradiction. Different categories: 3 *persons*, 1 *being*. (With a Muslim: the Quran comes in several transmitted readings, such as Hafs, Warsh and Qalun, and Muslims still say it is one Quran.)

universalTools.title: Context decides literal vs. figurative.
universalTools.text: Both sides agree personification exists. But personified things don't say "set apart for **me**" or "the work **I** have called them to."

universalTools.title: "Firstborn" = rank, not birth order.
universalTools.text: David was the *youngest* son and the *second* king, yet God calls him "firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth" (Ps 89:27).

holySpiritPlay.title: 🔥 THE HOLY SPIRIT PLAY: "the Spirit is Yahweh" (Unitarians, JWs, Oneness, Muslims)

intro.text: **Why this works:** Unitarians spend all their energy on Jesus (agency, *shaliach*, "a god"). They usually have **no prepared answer for the Spirit**. Two steps: **(A) the Spirit is a Person → (B) that Person is Yahweh.**

stepA.title: Step A: The Spirit is a *Who*, not a *what*

opener.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"*

rows.point: "Set apart for **me** Barnabas and Saul for the work to which **I** have called them." First-person speech, a choice, authority.
rows.question: *"Do actions have authority, or do persons?"* / *"He said 'I' and 'me' about Himself. That's self-awareness, right?"*

rows.point: "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit **and to us**." He takes part in a decision alongside the apostles.
rows.question: *"Can a force agree with a council?"*

rows.point: He can be grieved and rebelled against.
rows.question: *"An active force can't be offended. Whoever the Spirit is, He's someone you **can** offend."*

rows.point: He "does not speak on His own; whatever He **hears** He speaks."
rows.question: (vs. Oneness or "Spirit = the Father") *"Who is the Father hearing from?"*
*"Christ is called God's power and He's a person. So being God's power doesn't rule out being a person, right?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That's personification."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"I didn't ask about figurative language. Can He speak, yes or no? If I say 'my car told me it's not starting today,' did my car speak?"*. Then: personified wisdom never chooses missionaries in real time (Acts 13:2).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He just communicates information / He has no mouth."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"Does the Father have a mouth? Does the Father speak?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Father told the Spirit to say it."*
ifTheySay.youSay: The text says "for **me**… **I** have called." That's not quoting someone else.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He's rational energy, like AI."*
ifTheySay.youSay: AI is programmed. The Spirit wills, commands and is provoked. *"Can energy be rational without personhood?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"God used the Spirit's power to create."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God also created *through Christ* (John 1:3), and Christ is a person.

stepB.title: Step B: That Person is Yahweh

structure.text: an OT text says **Yahweh** spoke → the NT says **the Holy Spirit** said it.

rows.first: **2 Sam 23:2–3**: "The **Spirit of Yahweh** speaks by me… the God of Israel has said"
rows.second: **Acts 4:24–25**: the "Sovereign Lord… who **by the Holy Spirit**, through the mouth of David"
rows.note: Go-to question: *"So the Sovereign Lord who spoke through David is who?"*

rows.first: **Ps 95:7–11**: "They tested **Me**… I swore in **My** wrath" (Yahweh speaking)
rows.second: **Heb 3:7–11**: "As **the Holy Spirit says**… they tested **Me**… I swore in **My** wrath"
rows.note: *"Who is the Spirit talking about when He says 'they provoked **Me**'?"*

rows.first: **Isa 6:8–10**: the voice of **the Lord** (Yahweh of hosts, v.3–5) says "Go, and say to this people…"
rows.second: **Acts 28:25–26**: "**The Holy Spirit** was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah, 'Go to this people…'"
rows.note: Also John 12:41: Isaiah saw *Christ's* glory. One vision, three Persons.

rows.first: **Jer 31:31–34**: "This is the covenant **I** will make… **declares Yahweh**"
rows.second: **Heb 10:15–17**: "**The Holy Spirit** also bears witness… 'This is the covenant **I** will make'"
rows.note: The Spirit speaks Yahweh's covenant in the first person.

rows.first: **Acts 5:3–4**: "lie to **the Holy Spirit**" = "you have not lied to men but to **God**"

rows.second: The Spirit is the "Spirit of God" **and** the "Spirit of Christ"
rows.note: If the Spirit is Yahweh's own Spirit and also Christ's…

otOnly.label: Old Testament only (when they say "no NT")
otOnly.text: Deut 6:4 → Gen 1:2 (the Spirit of God) → 2 Sam 23:2–3 → Gen 31:11–13 / 35:1 (the Angel = the God of Bethel. *"Why is God saying 'go meet the God you met'?"*) → Zech 12:10 (*"they will look on **Me** whom they pierced." "Who did they pierce?"*). *"I don't need the New Testament to prove the Trinity."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The 'Spirit of Yahweh' means 'from Yahweh,' not 'is Yahweh.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"The answer is yes to all of them."* From Yahweh, and also Yahweh. Not either/or. Then: *"He's also the Spirit of Christ, right?"* (Rom 8:9). If they deny it, read the verse.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"OK, so the Spirit is just the Father."*
ifTheySay.youSay: John 16:13 (He hears from another), John 14:16 (*another* Helper whom the Father sends). *"Then the Father sends Himself and listens to Himself?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: They admit it but walk away from the Bible ("then I can't trust the Bible")
ifTheySay.youSay: that's 2 Tim 4:3, "itching ears." They are conceding the Bible teaches it.

closer.text: *"You've agreed the Spirit speaks, chooses, and is grieved, so He's a who. And Scripture says that Who is Yahweh. So Yahweh is more than one Person. Now let's talk about the Son."*

beliefs.text: Jehovah = the Father only. Jesus = Michael the Archangel, Jehovah's first creation, "a god." The Holy Spirit = God's impersonal "active force." The NWT is the authoritative translation; the Watchtower (Governing Body) is the "faithful and discreet slave."

lead.label: Their position
lead.text: Jehovah = the Father only. Jesus = Michael the Archangel, Jehovah's first creation, "a god." The Holy Spirit = God's impersonal "active force." The NWT is the authoritative translation; the Watchtower (Governing Body) is the "faithful and discreet slave."

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Who Jesus is. To them He is Michael, the first thing Jehovah made. Scripture says He is the Maker of all things, Yahweh the Son, and that unless a man believes He is who He says He is, he will die in his sins. With that comes how a man is saved: by faith in Christ alone, or by loyalty to an organization. (John 1:1–3; Col 1:16–17; John 8:24; Eph 2:8–9)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"In Hebrews 1:10 the Father says to the Son, 'You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth.' Those words come from Psalm 102, a prayer to Jehovah. Why does the Father speak to the Son with words written about Jehovah?"* (Heb 1:10–12; Ps 102:25–27)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: All things came into being through the Word, and apart from Him nothing came into being that has come into being, so He is not one of the things that came into being. Yahweh says He made all things alone. Isaiah saw Yahweh's glory, and John says Isaiah saw Jesus' glory. Thomas called Him "my Lord and my God," and Jesus blessed that confession. (John 1:3; Isa 44:24; Isa 6:1–5; John 12:41; John 20:28–29; Col 2:9)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"Jesus said, 'The Father is greater than I.'"* → Greater in position while the Son walked the earth as a servant, not greater in nature. A president is greater than I am in office and no more human than I am. The same Gospel says He made Himself equal with God, and that all are to honor the Son just as they honor the Father. (John 14:28; Phil 2:5–8; John 5:18; John 5:23)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"Do you know, right now, that you have eternal life?"* The Watchtower can only offer "maybe, if you stay faithful." Jesus says the one who believes has eternal life and has passed out of death into life. He did not say "Come to an organization." He said, "Come to Me." (John 5:24; 1 John 5:13; Rom 5:1; Matt 11:28)

lead.label: Get this first
lead.text: *"If the Bible disagrees with the Watchtower, you'd side with the Bible, right?"* Lock in that commitment before you open a verse.

cheatCard.text: **John 1:3**: "*not one thing* came into existence without Him" → *"So did Jesus create Himself?"*
**Col 1:16–17 (NWT)**: "all *other* things." The word "other" isn't in the Greek, and the Watchtower's own interlinear shows it.
**Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 / 22:13**: First and Last → *"Does being the First and Last mean you have a beginning?"*
**Heb 1:10–12 + Ps 102:25–27**: the Father addresses the Son with a Psalm spoken *to Jehovah* as Creator.
**Acts 13:2 + Heb 3:7–11**: the Spirit says "me / I," and the Spirit is the one tested in the wilderness → see [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play).
**Deut 18:21–22**: the 1914 / 1925 predictions → the test of a prophet.

chain.text: **John 1:3**: "All things came into existence through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into existence." *"Does it say 'except himself'?"*
*"If not one thing came into existence without Him, and Jesus came into existence, then Jehovah used Jesus to make Jesus?"*
**Col 1:16–17 (NWT)**: point out "all *other* things," four times. *"Where is 'other' in the Greek?"* It's *ta panta*, "all things." The Watchtower's **own Kingdom Interlinear** has no "other."

**Isa 44:24**: "I, Jehovah… stretched out the heavens **by myself**, who spread out the earth. **Who was with me?**" → *"If Jehovah created alone, and all things were created through Jesus, who is Jesus?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"'All' doesn't always mean all."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Here the verse defines it: "in the heavens and on the earth, visible and invisible, thrones, lordships" (Col 1:16). And John 1:3 says "not **one** thing."

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He was Jehovah's master worker (Prov 8:30)."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Working alongside doesn't mean created. And Prov 8 personifies Wisdom (a "she"). Is God ever without wisdom?

opener.text: *"According to John 1:3, how many things came into existence without the Word?"* (Answer: not one.)

closer.text: *"Everything that has ever come into existence came through Jesus. So Jesus has always existed. Do you agree?"*

chain.text: **Isa 44:6; 48:12**: Jehovah is "the first and the last; besides me there is no God."
**Rev 1:17–18**: "I am the First and the Last… I **became dead**." *"When did Jehovah die?"* So the speaker is Jesus.
**Rev 22:13, 16**: "Alpha and Omega, First and Last… I, **Jesus**." *"So Jesus has a beginning, but Jehovah doesn't, with the same title?"*

**Heb 1:8, 10–12**: the Father says to the Son, "You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth" — quoting **Ps 102:25–27**, which is addressed *to Jehovah*. *"Who is the Psalm talking to? And who does Hebrews apply it to?"*
**Isa 45:23 → Phil 2:10–11**: "To **me** every knee will bow" (Yahweh) → "at the name of **Jesus** every knee should bow."
**Isa 6:1–5 → John 12:41**: Isaiah "saw **his** [Jesus'] glory." The one Isaiah saw was Yahweh of hosts.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Jesus is the 'first and last' in a different sense."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"Then show me the text that makes the difference."* Same title, same book, same speaker formula.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Hebrews 1:8 should say 'God is your throne.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: v.8 opens "**to** the Son He says." The Father is speaking *to* the Son. And v.10 ("You, Lord…") has no throne issue at all.

opener.text: *"Who is the First and the Last in Isaiah 44:6?"* (They'll say Jehovah.) *"Does being the First and the Last mean you have a beginning?"* (No.)

closer.text: *"Jehovah says there's no God besides Him, and He gives His titles, His Psalm and His glory to Jesus. So either Jehovah shares His glory with a creature (Isa 42:8), or Jesus is Jehovah."*

offense.title: The Spirit is a Person and is Jehovah

opener.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"*

lead.text: → Run the full [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play). Best JW order: **Acts 13:2 → Eph 4:30 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 + Acts 4:24–25.** Witnesses often have no prepared answer at this point.

*"He didn't say 'I'm not good.' He asked a question to expose the man's thinking."*
*"If Jesus is good, what does that make Him?"*

opener.text: *"Is Jesus good?"* (They'll hesitate.)

offense.title: Only God can pay the ransom
offense.subtitle: Psalm 49

chain.text: **Ps 49:7–9**: no man can redeem his brother or give God a ransom for him. The redemption price for a soul is costly. *"How many men does the psalm say can pay it?"*
**Ps 49:15**: "But **God** will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol." *"So who does the psalmist say will do the redeeming?"*
**Isa 43:11**: Jehovah says, "there is no savior besides Me."
**Mark 10:45; 1 Tim 2:5–6**: Jesus came to give His life as a **ransom** for many. The one mediator gave Himself as a ransom for all.
**Titus 2:13–14**: our great **God and Savior**, Jesus Christ, gave Himself for us that He might **redeem** us.

**John 1:1; John 1:14; Heb 2:14–17**: the Word was God and became flesh. He **partook** of flesh and blood so that through death He might free those enslaved by the fear of death. He had to be man to die in our place, and God to redeem.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Psalm 49 is about imperfect men. Jesus was a perfect man, a corresponding ransom for Adam."*
ifTheySay.youSay: The psalm makes no exception for a perfect man. Its answer is "God will redeem." And every creature worships the Lamb for the people He purchased (Rev 5:9; Rev 5:13–14). *"Would Jehovah share that worship with a creature?"* (Isa 42:8)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Jehovah provided the ransom. Jesus was only the price."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Yes, the Father sent the Son. But the One who gave Himself is called our great God and Savior (Titus 2:13–14).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Acts 20:28 should read 'the blood of His own Son.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: That verse speaks of God purchasing the church with blood. Some manuscripts read "church of the Lord," and some translations say "the blood of His own." Don't rest the case on this one verse; the chain above stands without it.

opener.text: *"According to Psalm 49:7, can any man redeem his brother or give God a ransom for him?"* (They'll say no.)

summary.text: This is a cumulative case. Psalm 49 does not name Jesus, and it does not prove the Trinity on its own. It says no mere man can pay the ransom and that God will redeem. The New Testament then says Jesus paid it, and calls Him God.

closer.text: *"If no man can pay the ransom, and God says He will redeem, who is the Jesus who paid it?"*

defense.objection: "John 1:1 says 'a god.' No article = indefinite."
defense.response: A predicate noun before the verb without the article describes **nature** (Harner: qualitative). "The Word was God" in nature: all that God is, the Word was.
defense.goTo: John 1:1; **1 John 4:8** (*ho theos agapē estin*); **John 1:6** (*para theou*, no article)
defense.askBack: *"Is God 'a love'? Was John sent from 'a god'? Your NWT says 'God' in 1:6. Why not in 1:1?"*

defense.objection: "*Ton theon* = the Almighty; *theos* = a lesser god."
defense.response: That's just Greek case. *Ton theon* is accusative after *pros*; *theos* is nominative. Case endings aren't ranks.
defense.askBack: *"Is the Father a lesser god when he's in the nominative?"*

defense.objection: "Firstborn of creation" (Col 1:15) = first created
defense.response: *Prōtotokos* = preeminent heir. v.16 gives the reason: "**because** by Him all things were created."
defense.askBack: *"Who was Israel's first king? Saul. So how is David 'firstborn' of the kings?"*

defense.objection: "Only-begotten" (John 3:16) = uniquely created
defense.response: *Monogenēs* = the unique, only begotten Son, never "created" (Heb 11:17: Isaac wasn't Abraham's only son).
defense.askBack: *"Was Isaac Abraham's only child?"*

defense.objection: "Beginning of the creation of God" (Rev 3:14)
defense.response: *Archē* = origin / ruler / source. He's where creation comes from.
defense.askBack: *"If you're the originator of your business, aren't you its origin?"*

defense.objection: "John 5:19: Jesus can do nothing on his own"
defense.response: That shows the Persons are distinct and act together. Finish the verse: "whatever the Father does, **the Son does likewise**."
defense.askBack: *"Does the Father do anything without the Son?"*

defense.objection: "John 14:28: 'the Father is greater than I'"
defense.response: Greater in role, in the Son's humbled human state. Not in nature. Phil 2:6–7.
defense.askBack: *"Is a husband 'greater' in nature than his wife because he leads?"*

defense.objection: "Psalm 8 / Heb 2: everything is subject to *man*, not Jesus"
defense.response: Heb 2:9 identifies the "him": "**namely Jesus**."
defense.askBack: *"Who are we going to trust, you or the author of Hebrews?"*

defense.objection: "Daniel 7: Jesus wasn't seated / Rev 3:21: believers sit on the throne too"
defense.response: Sharing kingdom authority ≠ sitting **on high** in heaven, the place that belongs to Yahweh alone (Ps 113:5).
defense.askBack: *"Show me anyone other than Jesus who sits 'on high' at the right hand of the Majesty."*

defense.objection: "Holy Spirit = active force"
defense.response: → [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play)
defense.askBack: *"Can a force be grieved?"*

defense.objection: "Trinity isn't in the Bible."
defense.response: Word–concept fallacy. "Jehovah's Witness" isn't in the Bible as a denomination name either. Is the *concept* taught?
defense.askBack: *"Is the word 'theocracy' in the Bible?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus is Michael the Archangel."
defense.response: Scripture never says it. Michael did not dare rebuke Satan himself (Jude 9); Jesus commands him directly (Matt 4:10). God never called any angel "My Son," and **all** the angels worship the Son.
defense.askBack: *"To which of the angels did God ever say, 'You are My Son'?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was raised as a spirit, not in a body."
defense.response: He said a spirit does not have flesh and bones as He has, He showed His wounds, and He said He would raise **His body**.
defense.askBack: *"In John 2:19–21, what did Jesus say He would raise?"*

defense.objection: "Only 144,000 go to heaven."
defense.response: Right after the 144,000, John sees a great multitude **no one could count** standing before the throne, serving God in His temple.
defense.askBack: *"Where is the great multitude standing in Rev 7:9?"*

defense.objection: "The dead are unconscious. The soul stops existing."
defense.response: Paul expected to depart and **be with Christ**, away from the body and at home with the Lord. The souls under the altar speak.
defense.askBack: *"How do the souls in Rev 6:10 cry out if they don't exist?"*

defense.objection: "Hell isn't eternal. The wicked are simply destroyed."
defense.response: Jesus uses the same word, "eternal," for the punishment and for the life in one sentence.
defense.askBack: *"If the punishment isn't eternal, is the life?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus died on a stake, not a cross."
defense.response: Don't make this the fight. Thomas speaks of **nails**, plural, in His hands, and the sign was placed above His **head**. Then go back to who Jesus is.
defense.askBack: *"Why 'nails,' plural, for His hands?"*

defense.objection: "You must use God's name, Jehovah."
defense.response: The apostles take the Old Testament "name" texts and apply them to **Jesus**. Joel's "call on the name of Yahweh" becomes confessing Jesus as Lord.
defense.askBack: *"In Rom 10:13, whose name is in view, given verse 9?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus is a god, a mighty one, but not the true God."
defense.response: Jehovah says no god was formed before or after Him and He knows of no other. So is Jesus a true God or a false god? Thomas calls Him "my Lord and **my God**" and Jesus accepts it.
defense.askBack: *"Is Jesus a true god or a false god?"*

defense.objection: "People only did obeisance to Jesus, not worship."
defense.response: All the angels worship the Son. Every creature gives the same honor to God and to the Lamb. An angel refuses it; Jesus receives it.
defense.askBack: *"Why does the angel refuse what Jesus accepts?"*

defense.objection: "You need Jehovah's organization to be saved."
defense.response: Salvation is by grace through faith, not works, and not membership. When others left, Peter did not ask **where** to go, but **to whom**.
defense.askBack: *"To whom did Peter say we should go?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was a perfect man, a corresponding ransom for Adam. He didn't need to be God."
defense.response: He had to be truly man to die in our place. But Scripture says no man can ransom another, and that God Himself redeems. The One who paid is the Word, who was God and became flesh. Run [Only God can pay the ransom](/jw/case/play-6).
defense.askBack: *"Psalm 49 says no man can pay it. So what kind of man is Jesus?"*

beliefs.text: Yahweh = the Father alone, one person. Jesus = a human Messiah (Biblical Unitarian) or a created spirit being (Arian). No real pre-existence. Jesus is God's "agent" (*shaliach*), so whatever He says or does as God is "agency." The Spirit = God's power or presence, not a person.

lead.label: Their position
lead.text: Yahweh = the Father alone, one person. Jesus = a human Messiah (Biblical Unitarian) or a created spirit being (Arian). No real pre-existence. Jesus is God's "agent" (*shaliach*), so whatever He says or does as God is "agency." The Spirit = God's power or presence, not a person.

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Whether Jesus is a man God empowered, or the eternal Son who became man. If He is only a creature, worshiping Him is idolatry and His death cannot pay for the sins of the world. Scripture says the Word was God and became flesh. (John 1:1; John 1:14; Phil 2:5–8; Heb 1:3)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"Yahweh says He will not give His glory to another. Then how did Jesus share the Father's glory before the world was, and why does every creature worship the Lamb together with the One on the throne?"* (Isa 42:8; John 17:5; Rev 5:13–14)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: The Word was with God and was God, and all things were made through Him. Before Abraham was born, "I am." The Father says to the Son, "Your throne, O God, is forever." Thomas calls Him "my Lord and my God." And the Spirit is a person who can be lied to, and to lie to Him is to lie to God. (John 1:1–3; John 8:58; Heb 1:8–10; John 20:28; Acts 5:3–4)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"Jesus calls the Father 'the only true God' (John 17:3)."* → He does, and in the same sentence eternal life is knowing the Father and Jesus Christ, and two verses later He speaks of glory He had with the Father before the world was. Calling the Father the only true God no more shuts out the Son than calling Jesus "our only Master and Lord" shuts out the Father. John himself calls the Son the true God. (John 17:3–5; Jude 1:4; 1 John 5:20)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"If Jesus is only a man, how can one man's death pay for the sins of the world?"* No mere man can redeem his brother. God purchased the church with His own blood, and because the Son lives forever He saves forever those who draw near to God through Him. (Ps 49:7–8; Acts 20:28; Heb 7:25; John 8:24)

lead.label: Their weak spot
lead.text: **the Holy Spirit** and the **Angel of Yahweh**. Go there early.

defense.objection: **The syllogism:** "YHWH is the Most High; Jesus is the Son of the Most High; if Jesus is YHWH, Jesus is his own Father."
defense.response: Equivocation. You're treating "Yahweh" as naming only one person. Scripture applies the name to the **Father, the Son and the Spirit**. Jesus is Yahweh, and He is not the person of the Father.
defense.goTo: Gen 19:24 (Yahweh rains fire *from* Yahweh); Judges 1:1–2 ("Judah" = man or tribe)
defense.askBack: *"Is 'Judah' a person or a tribe?"*

defense.objection: "John 17:3: the Father is 'the only true God'"
defense.response: Yes, the Father is the only true God. Trinitarians agree. "Only" excludes **false gods**, not the Son: the same John calls Jesus "the true God" (1 John 5:20).
defense.goTo: 1 John 5:20; Jude 4 ("our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ")
defense.askBack: *"Jude calls Jesus our 'only Lord.' Does that make the Father not Lord?"*

defense.objection: "1 Cor 8:6: one God, the Father"
defense.response: Same verse: "one **Lord**, Jesus Christ." Paul splits the Shema (Deut 6:4) between Father and Son. If "one God, the Father" excludes Jesus from being God, "one Lord, Jesus" excludes the Father from being Lord.
defense.askBack: *"Is the Father not Lord?"*

defense.objection: "God is not a man" (Num 23:19; Hos 11:9)

defense.askBack: *"Can the God who made human nature add it to Himself?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus died, and God can't die"
defense.response: The Person of the Son died **in His human nature**. The divine nature doesn't die. Two natures, one Person.
defense.askBack: *"Who was crucified in 1 Cor 2:8?"*

defense.objection: "*Homoousios* / Nicaea / the church invented it"
defense.response: The term is a summary of biblical teaching, not new revelation. Answer from the text, not from church history.
defense.askBack: *"Fine. Set Nicaea aside. Let's just read Rev 3:14 / John 1:3."*

defense.objection: "*Archē* (Rev 3:14) = first creature" / "Abba means source"
defense.response: *Archē* = origin / ruler / active cause. The NT is Greek, not Hebrew, and *Abba* means "Father."
defense.askBack: *"Does the software exist before you made it?"*

defense.objection: "Context limits 'Author of life' / 'all things'"

defense.objection: "Jesus has a God (John 20:17), so He isn't God."

defense.askBack: *"In Heb 1:8–9, who is called God, and who is His God?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus didn't know the day or the hour (Mark 13:32)."
defense.response: Two natures. As man He grew in wisdom; as God He knows all things.
defense.askBack: *"How can Peter say, 'Lord, You know all things'?"*

defense.objection: "God cannot be tempted (James 1:13), but Jesus was."
defense.response: He was tempted **as man**, from outside, and never sinned. That is the point of the incarnation: a true human High Priest.
defense.askBack: *"Did the temptation ever find sin in Him?"*

defense.objection: "No one has ever seen God, but people saw Jesus."
defense.response: Finish the verse: the only begotten **God** has explained Him. No one has seen the Father apart from the Son. And Isaiah saw Yahweh, and John says he saw Christ's glory.
defense.askBack: *"Who did Isaiah see in the temple?"*

defense.objection: "Philippians 2 only says Jesus didn't grasp at being equal with God."
defense.response: He was **existing in the form of God** and then **took** the form of a slave. You cannot take on humanity if you were only ever human.
defense.askBack: *"When did He 'take' the form of a slave, if He was only ever a man?"*

defense.objection: "The 'Word' in John 1 is God's plan, not a person."
defense.response: The Word is **with** God, makes all things, becomes flesh, and shares glory with the Father before the world existed. Plans don't do that.
defense.askBack: *"Can a plan share glory with the Father before the world existed?"*

defense.objection: "'Before Abraham was, I am' just means He was foreordained."
defense.response: His hearers understood Him. They picked up stones. Nobody is stoned for being part of God's plan.
defense.askBack: *"Why did they try to stone Him?"*

defense.objection: "Thomas was only exclaiming in surprise (John 20:28)."
defense.response: The text says Thomas said it **to Him**, and Jesus blesses the confession instead of rebuking it.
defense.askBack: *"Does Jesus correct Thomas or commend him?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus is called 'god' the way judges and Moses were."

defense.objection: "Matthew 28:19 was added later."

defense.askBack: *"Which manuscript leaves it out?"*

defense.objection: "There is one mediator, 'the man Christ Jesus' (1 Tim 2:5). A sinless man was enough."

Hebrews says He **partook** of flesh and blood, and you cannot take on what you already only are. A mediator between God and men stands on both sides.
defense.askBack: *"Hebrews 2:14 says He partook of flesh and blood. Who was He before He did?"*

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: Yahweh says He is the first and the last, that there is no God besides Him, and that He does not know of any other. From everlasting to everlasting He is God. God is not a man. God is spirit. He does not change. (Isa 44:6, 8; Isa 45:5; Ps 90:2; Num 23:19; John 4:24; Mal 3:6)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"I have a testimony. I prayed about the Book of Mormon and I know it is true."* → I don't doubt you felt something. But Scripture says the heart is deceitful, tells us to test the spirits, and says that even an angel from heaven preaching another gospel is to be rejected. The Bereans were called noble for checking Paul against the Scriptures, not against their feelings. (Jer 17:9; 1 John 4:1; Gal 1:8; Acts 17:11)

defense.objection: "We are saved by grace after all we can do (2 Nephi 25:23)."

defense.objection: "The Bible is true only as far as it is translated correctly. Plain and precious things were lost."

defense.objection: "We have a living prophet today."

defense.objection: "Jesus and Lucifer are spirit brothers."

defense.askBack: *"If Jesus made everything invisible in heaven, who made Lucifer?"*

defense.objection: "We all lived as spirits with God before we were born."

defense.askBack: *"Who does Jesus say is from above, and who is from below?"*

defense.objection: "The priesthood was restored through Joseph Smith."
defense.response: The Aaronic priesthood was set aside, and Jesus holds His priesthood **permanently**. Every believer is already part of a royal priesthood.
defense.askBack: *"If Jesus holds it permanently, who else needs to?"*

defense.objection: "Families are forever through temple marriage."

defense.objection: "There are three degrees of glory. Almost everyone is saved somewhere."
defense.response: Jesus speaks of two roads and two ends: eternal punishment or eternal life.
defense.askBack: *"How many destinations does Jesus name?"*

defense.objection: "We're Christians too. We believe in Jesus."

defense.askBack: *"Is the Jesus you trust the eternal Creator, or a being who became a god?"*

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: Asked under oath whether He is the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One, Jesus said, "I am," and claimed to be the Son of Man who comes on the clouds. They condemned Him for blasphemy. He said, "Before Abraham was born, I am." He said He came to give His life as a ransom. The earliest eyewitness testimony is that He died, was buried, was raised and was seen. (Mark 14:61–64; John 8:58; Mark 10:45; 1 Cor 15:3–8; John 20:28)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"The Bible has been corrupted."* → The Quran itself points Jews and Christians of Muhammad's day to the Torah and the Gospel they had in their hands (Q 5:43; Q 5:47; Q 5:68; Q 10:94). We have copies of those books from centuries before Muhammad, and they say what our Bibles say today. So when was it corrupted? See [Is the Bible reliable?](/topic/is-the-bible-reliable).

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"How do you know your good deeds will outweigh your bad? Can you be sure of paradise?"* A just judge cannot simply overlook guilt. God showed His love in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us, so that He is both just and the justifier. Eternal life is a gift, and God wants you to know you have it. (Rom 3:26; Rom 5:8; Rom 6:23; 1 John 5:13)

summary.text: The Quran says the Torah and Gospel in Christians' and Jews' hands in the 7th century were God's word and confirmed them. We have the 7th-century Bible (and far older manuscripts: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Dead Sea Scrolls). That Bible says Jesus is the Son of God, died and rose. **Either** the Bible is reliable, and it contradicts the Quran → Islam is false. **Or** the Bible is corrupted, and then the Quran confirmed a corrupted book → Islam is false. Either way, Islam fails.

opener.text: *"You say Islam is morally superior. Can we read a few verses of the Quran and see?"*

defense.objection: "How can God be 3 and 1?"
defense.response: Three in one sense (**Persons**), one in another (**Being**). Different categories, no contradiction.
defense.askBack: *"The Quran has several transmitted readings: Hafs, Warsh, Qalun. Is that three Qurans, or one?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus never said 'I am God, worship me.'"
defense.response: He said things only God could say, and accepted what only God receives. Watch for the goalpost shift.
defense.askBack: *"First you wanted a verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' mouth?"*

defense.objection: "God is not a man" (Hosea 11:9)
defense.response: Correct by nature. The Son **added** a human nature. Two natures, one Person. And don't let them skip the verse you gave first.
defense.askBack: *"Do you acknowledge Heb 1:3 says the Son is the exact imprint of God's nature?"*

defense.objection: "Which God sent Jesus? Who was He praying to?"
defense.response: One God, three Persons. The **Father** sent the **Son**. Jesus prayed as a true man.
defense.askBack: *"In John 17:5 Jesus asks for the glory He had with the Father before the world existed. Can a mere prophet pray that?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus wasn't crucified" (Q 4:157)
defense.response: Every early source, Christian and non-Christian (Josephus c. AD 93, Tacitus c. AD 116), agrees He was crucified. The Quran denies it 600 years later with no source. And the Injil the Quran confirms teaches it.
defense.askBack: *"Who did Allah make look like Jesus, and did he deceive the disciples into starting Christianity?"*

defense.objection: "Paul corrupted Jesus' message."
defense.response: Paul's gospel was checked and approved by Peter, James and John. And Q 61:14 praises Jesus' disciples as Allah's helpers, who won.
defense.askBack: *"Q 61:14 says Allah made Jesus' followers victorious. The faith that won taught what Paul taught. Did Allah back the wrong side?"*

defense.objection: "The Torah is one book, but you have five."
defense.response: The Torah = Genesis to Deuteronomy, the five books of Moses: one Torah in five scrolls. Jewish tradition says Joshua added the account of Moses' death (Deut 34).
defense.askBack: *"The Quran has 114 surahs. Is it 114 books, or one?"*

defense.objection: "The Trinity is pagan / Allah is 'the third of three'"
defense.response: The Quran pictures worship of God, Jesus and **Mary** (Q 5:116; cf. Q 5:73–75). That is not the Trinity Christians believe: one God in three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
defense.askBack: *"Which Christian ever taught Mary is part of the Trinity?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus ate, slept and prayed. God doesn't do that."
defense.response: He is truly God and truly man. The Word **became flesh**. Hunger and sleep belong to His human nature; they don't cancel His divine nature.
defense.askBack: *"If God chose to enter His creation as a man, who could stop Him?"*

defense.objection: "The Injil was one book given to Jesus. You have four, written by men."
defense.response: "Gospel" means the good news about Jesus. And the Quran tells the people of the Gospel to judge by what they **had** in the 7th century, which was these four.
defense.askBack: *"What Gospel did Christians have in Muhammad's day?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel."
defense.response: His earthly ministry went to Israel first, as promised. Then He sent His disciples to **all nations**, as Isaiah foretold.
defense.askBack: *"Who does Jesus send them to in Matt 28:19?"*

defense.objection: "The Bible has contradictions and too many versions."
defense.response: Translations are not different Bibles. The manuscript differences are known and printed in the footnotes, and no teaching depends on them. Ask for one and read it together.
defense.askBack: *"Which contradiction? Let's read it."*

defense.objection: "God can simply forgive. He doesn't need a sacrifice."
defense.response: A judge who lets the guilty go is unjust. God will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. At the cross He is both **just and the justifier**. Even the Quran ransoms Abraham's son with a great sacrifice.
defense.askBack: *"If a judge lets the guilty go free, is he a just judge?"*

defense.objection: "No one can carry another person's sins (Q 6:164)."
defense.response: The Torah the Quran confirms is built on substitution: the sins of the people laid on another. Isaiah foretold One who would bear the iniquity of us all. And Jesus is not an unwilling bystander punished for a stranger. He is the Son who laid down His life of His own accord, as the Father purposed.
defense.askBack: *"What does Isaiah 53:6 say Yahweh laid on Him?"*

defense.objection: "Your own Bible says each person dies for his own sin (Deut 24:16; Ezek 18:20)."
defense.response: Deuteronomy tells human courts not to execute a son for his father's crime. Ezekiel says God holds each person to account for his own sin. Both forbid punishing an unwilling innocent. Neither forbids a willing substitute whom God Himself appoints. The same Law commands the sacrifices, and Isaiah foretells the Servant who bears the sin of many.
defense.askBack: *"If substitution is forbidden, what are the sacrifices in Leviticus for?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was only a prophet. A prophet can't redeem anyone."
defense.response: Agreed: no mere man can. The Psalms say no man can ransom his brother, and that God Himself will redeem. That is why the Redeemer had to be God become man. Jesus said He came to give His life as a ransom.
defense.askBack: *"If no man can pay the ransom, who can?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus and His disciples were Muslims."
defense.response: His disciples worshiped Him, called Him Lord and God, and preached that He was crucified and raised.
defense.askBack: *"Would a Muslim say 'My Lord and my God' to Jesus?"*

defense.objection: "Muhammad is named in Song of Songs 5:16."
defense.response: The Hebrew word there is an ordinary word for "desirable," used by a bride about her beloved. The same word family describes Ezekiel's wife (Ezek 24:16) and Israel's children (Hos 9:16).
defense.askBack: *"Is Muhammad also in Ezekiel 24:16, where the same word is used?"*

defense.objection: "Islam is the fastest-growing religion, so it must be true."
defense.response: Truth isn't a headcount. Jesus said the many take the wide road.
defense.askBack: *"Is something true because many people believe it?"*

defense.objection: "The Quran is a miracle. No one can produce a chapter like it."
defense.response: That test has no judge and no standard. The Quran gives a better test: check with those who read the Scripture before.
defense.askBack: *"Who judges the contest, and by what standard?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus said, 'Why do you call Me good? Only God is good.'"
defense.response: He didn't say He isn't good. He asked the man **why** he said it. Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd.
defense.askBack: *"Is Jesus good?"*

beliefs.text: There is one God, He gave the Torah to Israel at Sinai, and Israel is His covenant people. The Messiah has not come yet: he will be a human king from David's line who gathers Israel, rebuilds the temple and brings peace to the world, and Jesus did none of that. Man is not born guilty and is able to choose good. Sin is forgiven through repentance, prayer and deeds of charity, with Yom Kippur at the centre. Know who you are talking to: in America about 9% of Jewish people are Orthodox, 37% Reform, 17% Conservative, and 32% claim no branch at all [Pew, Jewish Americans in 2020]. Many have never read Isaiah.

lead.label: Their position
lead.text: There is one God, He gave the Torah to Israel at Sinai, and Israel is His covenant people. The Messiah has not come yet: he will be a human king from David's line who gathers Israel, rebuilds the temple and brings peace to the world, and Jesus did none of that. Man is not born guilty and is able to choose good. Sin is forgiven through repentance, prayer and deeds of charity, with Yom Kippur at the centre. Know who you are talking to: in America about 9% of Jewish people are Orthodox, 37% Reform, 17% Conservative, and 32% claim no branch at all [Pew, Jewish Americans in 2020]. Many have never read Isaiah.

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Whether a person needs a Savior from sin, and whether Jesus is that Savior, the promised Messiah. John MacArthur: "Judaism doesn't need a savior from sin. Christianity exalts the Savior from sin" [MacArthur, sermon introducing Isaiah 53]. If keeping, repenting and suffering can make a man right with God, a Messiah who dies in the sinner's place has no purpose. Scripture says no one living is righteous before God, and that the Servant bears the sin of many. (Ps 143:2; Isa 64:6; Isa 53:5–6; Isa 53:11)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"Do you, personally, need a Savior to take your place and bear God's judgment for your sins?"* (Isa 53:6)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: Stay in their own Scriptures. Seven hundred years before Jesus, Isaiah described a righteous Servant who is rejected by his own people, pierced for their transgressions, killed, buried with a rich man, alive again to see his offspring, and who makes many righteous by bearing their sins. Moses said it is the blood that makes atonement. Daniel said the Anointed One would be cut off before the city and the temple were destroyed, and that happened in AD 70. (Isa 53:5–6; Isa 53:8–11; Lev 17:11; Dan 9:26; Zech 12:10)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"The servant in Isaiah 53 is the nation of Israel."* → Israel is called God's servant earlier in the book, but this Servant restores Israel, so he cannot be Israel. He is innocent, and Isaiah opens his book calling Israel a sinful nation. He suffers silently and willingly, for "my people," as a guilt offering. The oldest Jewish readings took him to be the Messiah [Targum Jonathan on Isa 52:13; Talmud, Sanhedrin 98b]. (Isa 49:5–6; Isa 53:8–9; Isa 1:4; Isa 53:10)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"Abraham told Isaac, 'God will provide for Himself the lamb.' Isaiah says the Servant was led like a lamb to slaughter, and that Yahweh laid on him the iniquity of us all. If God has provided the Lamb, what will you do with Him?"* Abraham believed God and it was counted to him as righteousness. The same promise stands for the Jew first. (Gen 22:8; Isa 53:6–7; Gen 15:6; Rom 1:16; Rom 10:9–13)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: There is one God, the Maker of heaven and earth, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. The Law, the Prophets and the Writings are His word. God chose Israel, has kept them through every attempt to destroy them, and is not finished with them. Sin is real and must be confessed to God. A Messiah from David's line is promised. Every writer of the New Testament but perhaps one was Jewish, and so is Jesus.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: Come with love and a debt of thanks: the Scriptures, the covenants and the Messiah came to us through them. MacArthur told Ben Shapiro, "I am a Christian because of the Old Testament" [MacArthur, interview with Ben Shapiro]. Paul had great sorrow and unceasing grief for his kinsmen and prayed for their salvation, and so should you. Never say "the Jews killed Jesus" as a charge against the person in front of you: Jews and Gentiles together did what God's hand had decided beforehand, and Jesus laid down His life of His own accord. Own the history honestly: terrible things were done to Jewish people in the name of Christ, against everything Christ taught. Do not be arrogant toward the branches; you stand by faith. Use the Old Testament first, ask them to read the passage aloud, and ask "Who is this about?" before you say a word. The hope is sure. MacArthur: "God's not through with them" [MacArthur, conference message on Israel's future]. (Rom 9:1–5; Rom 10:1; Acts 4:27–28; John 10:17–18; Rom 11:18–20; Rom 11:25–27)

altOpeners.text: *"I'm a Christian because of the Hebrew Scriptures. Can I show you the chapter that did it?"*

chain.text: **Isa 52:13–15**: The passage starts here, three verses before the chapter break. God says, "Behold, My Servant." He will be exalted, yet his appearance is marred more than any man. *"Have you read this before?"*
**Isa 53:1–3**: He grows up like a root out of dry ground, with nothing to draw anyone to him. He is despised and rejected by his own people. *"Who is the 'we' that did not esteem him?"*

**Isa 53:4–6**: He is pierced for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities. All of us like sheep have gone astray, and Yahweh laid on him the iniquity of us all. *"Is he suffering for his own sins, or for someone else's?"*

**Isa 53:7–9**: He is silent like a lamb led to slaughter, cut off from the land of the living for the transgression of "my people," given a grave with the wicked yet with a rich man in his death, though he had done no violence and spoken no deceit. *"If he dies for 'my people,' can he be the people?"*
**Isa 53:10**: Yahweh was pleased to crush him, and he gives himself as a guilt offering. Then he sees his offspring and prolongs his days. *"How does a dead man prolong his days?"*
**Isa 53:11–12**: The Righteous One, My Servant, will justify the many, for he will bear their iniquities. *"How does one man's suffering make many people righteous?"*

**Acts 8:32–35**: An official from Ethiopia was reading this very passage and asked whom the prophet meant. Philip began from that Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus. That is the pattern.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The servant is Israel."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Isaiah does call Israel God's servant (Isa 41:8), a servant he then calls blind and deaf (Isa 42:19). But in Isa 49:5–6 the Servant is the one who brings Jacob back and raises up the tribes of Israel. One restores the other. And this Servant is innocent (Isa 53:9), while Isaiah's Israel is "a people weighed down with iniquity" (Isa 1:4). *"When did Israel suffer silently, willingly and sinlessly, to pay for someone else's sins?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That is a Christian reading."*
ifTheySay.youSay: The Aramaic Targum, read in synagogues, renders Isa 52:13 "Behold, My servant the Messiah" [Targum Jonathan]. The Talmud gives Messiah a name from Isa 53:4 [Sanhedrin 98b]. Reading the servant as the nation became the standard answer with Rashi, in the eleventh century, a thousand years after Jesus. *"Why did the reading change?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"We never read that in synagogue."*
ifTheySay.youSay: That is true. The weekly readings from the Prophets stop at Isa 52:12 and pick up again at Isa 54:1. Don't accuse anyone of hiding it. Just say, *"Then let's read it now."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He was just a man who died. Many Jews were crucified."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Only one was foretold as dying for others' sins, buried in a rich man's tomb, and alive afterward. Go to [The resurrection](/topic/the-resurrection).

opener.text: *"Would you read a passage from the prophet Isaiah with me and tell me who you think it describes?"*

closer.text: *"Isaiah wrote it in the past tense, as Israel looking back and saying, 'We thought God had struck him, but he was pierced for our transgressions.' Zechariah says that day is coming for the whole nation. It can be today for you."* (Zech 12:10; Zech 13:1; Isa 53:4–5)

altOpeners.text: *"The Torah gives a whole book to sacrifice. Since the temple fell, what takes its place, and who said so?"*

chain.text: **Isa 1:4–6; Isa 59:2**: Isaiah begins by telling the covenant people they are a sinful nation, sick from head to foot, and that their iniquities have separated them from God. Being Abraham's child did not exempt them. *"Was Isaiah wrong about them, or is he right about all of us?"*

**Ps 143:2; Eccl 7:20; Isa 64:6**: No one living is righteous before God. There is not a righteous man on earth who never sins. Our righteous deeds are like a filthy garment. *"If the good deeds are stained too, what do you bring?"*
**Lev 17:11**: The life of the flesh is in the blood, and God gave it on the altar to make atonement. *"God chose the means. Can we choose another?"*

**Lev 16:15–16, 21–22**: On the Day of Atonement one goat dies and the sins of the people are confessed over the head of the other, which carries them away. An innocent substitute bears the guilt. *"Where is that substitute today?"*

**Dan 9:26**: The Anointed One is cut off and has nothing, and then the city and the sanctuary are destroyed. The temple has been gone since AD 70. *"Would God take away the sacrifices and leave nothing in their place?"*
**Isa 53:10**: The Servant gives himself as a guilt offering. The animal sacrifices were pictures; he is what they pictured. (Heb 10:4; Heb 10:11–14)
**Jer 31:31–34**: God promised a new covenant, not like the one made at Sinai, in which He forgives iniquity and remembers sin no more. *"Has that covenant come? Through whom?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Repentance, prayer and charity atone now."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Scripture commands all three, and never says they replace the blood. Daniel repented and prayed in exile, and still confessed that he had no righteousness of his own to plead, only God's great compassion (Dan 9:18). *"Where does God say He changed the means of atonement?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"God doesn't want sacrifice. Hosea 6:6, Psalm 51:16."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Those verses rebuke sacrifice offered with a heart far from God. David's psalm ends with God delighting in righteous sacrifices on His altar (Ps 51:19). God was not cancelling Leviticus; He was demanding a broken heart with it.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The prayers of our lips replace the bulls. Hosea 14:2."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Hosea calls Israel to return with words of confession. He does not say words pay for sin. Someone still has to bear it. (Isa 53:6)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I'm a good person. I keep the commandments."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Ask which one they have kept perfectly, and walk through a few. Go to [The Way of the Master](/topic/the-way-of-the-master). The Law was given to show sin, and Moses himself said the people would not keep it. (Deut 31:27–29; Deut 27:26)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I'm Jewish. I'm already in the covenant."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Isaiah, Jeremiah and John the Baptist all preached repentance to people in the covenant. God requires a circumcised heart. (Deut 10:16; Jer 4:4; Matt 3:9; Rom 2:28–29)

opener.text: *"On Yom Kippur, how do you know your sins are actually forgiven?"*

closer.text: *"Abraham was counted righteous before he had done anything, because he believed God. Habakkuk says the righteous will live by faith. God has provided the sacrifice Himself. Will you trust Him?"* (Gen 15:6; Hab 2:4; Isa 53:11)

offense.subtitle: when he comes, what he does, who he is

altOpeners.text: *"If the Messiah had already come, how would you know?"*

chain.text: **Mic 5:2**: He is born in Bethlehem, and his goings forth are from long ago, from the days of eternity. *"What kind of man has origins from eternity?"*
**Isa 9:6–7**: A child is born, a son is given, who sits on David's throne forever, and his name is Mighty God. *"Is that title ever given to a mere man?"*
**Ps 110:1**: David calls his own descendant "my Lord," and Yahweh seats him at His right hand. *"Why would David call his son 'Lord'?"* (Matt 22:41–46)
**Dan 7:13–14**: One like a Son of Man comes with the clouds of heaven, and all peoples serve him in a kingdom that never ends. That service belongs to God alone.
**Zech 9:9**: Your king comes to you humble, riding on a donkey. **Dan 7:13**: he comes on the clouds. *"How can both be true of one Messiah?"* Two comings: first to suffer, then to reign.

**Dan 9:24–26**: He comes to atone for iniquity, he is cut off, and then the temple is destroyed. *"The temple was destroyed in AD 70. Who came before that, claimed to be Messiah, died, and is worshiped by a billion Gentiles as Isaiah 49:6 said?"*
**Zech 12:10**: God pours out the Spirit of grace on the house of David, and "they will look on Me whom they have pierced" and mourn as for an only son. The One pierced is the One speaking.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Messiah brings world peace. There is no peace, so Jesus is not the Messiah."*
ifTheySay.youSay: He will bring it. The prophets give two pictures, a suffering Servant and a reigning King, and the rabbis saw the tension themselves and proposed two Messiahs, one of whom is killed [Talmud, Sukkah 52a]. Scripture's answer is one Messiah who comes twice. He dealt with sin first, because peace with God has to come before peace on earth. (Isa 53:5; Isa 2:4; Zech 14:4, 9)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"God is not a man. Numbers 23:19."*
ifTheySay.youSay: That verse says God does not lie or change His mind the way a man does. It does not say God cannot take on flesh. He appeared to Abraham and ate with him (Gen 18:1–2), and Isaiah calls the child born "Mighty God" (Isa 9:6).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Messiah is a man, not God."*
ifTheySay.youSay: He is both. Go to [The Trinity](/topic/the-trinity) and use Ps 110:1, Isa 9:6 and Dan 7:13–14 from this play.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Isaiah 7:14 says 'young woman,' not 'virgin.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: The word is *almah*, a young unmarried woman, and Jewish translators before Jesus was born rendered it in Greek with the word for virgin [Septuagint]. A young woman giving birth is no sign at all. But don't make this your lead text; Isaiah 53 and Daniel 9 carry more weight in this conversation.

opener.text: *"What do you think the Messiah will do when he comes, and how will you recognize him?"*

closer.text: *"Moses said God would raise up a Prophet like him, and that God would hold accountable anyone who would not listen to him. I believe He has come. Would you read the Gospel of Matthew, written by a Jew for Jews, and see whether Jesus is the one Moses and the prophets wrote about?"* (Deut 18:15, 18–19; John 5:46)

defense.objection: "The servant in Isaiah 53 is Israel."
defense.response: This Servant restores Israel, is sinless, suffers willingly and dies for "my people." None of that fits the nation Isaiah calls sinful. The oldest Jewish readings took him to be Messiah [Targum Jonathan; Sanhedrin 98b]. Run Play 1.
defense.askBack: *"If he dies for the people, how can he be the people?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus didn't bring peace, so he isn't the Messiah."
defense.response: The prophets show Messiah suffering and Messiah reigning. One Messiah, two comings. He dealt with sin first; He will reign on David's throne and the nations will learn war no more.
defense.askBack: *"Which does a sinner need first: peace on earth, or peace with God?"*

defense.objection: "'Hear, O Israel, the LORD is one.' The Trinity is idolatry."
defense.response: We confess the Shema. One God, one Being. The Hebrew Scriptures themselves show more: "Let Us make man," Yahweh sending His Servant and His Spirit, and David's Lord seated beside Yahweh. See [The Trinity](/topic/the-trinity).
defense.askBack: *"Who is David's 'Lord' in Psalm 110?"*

defense.objection: "God is not a man."
defense.response: Numbers 23:19 says God does not lie like a man. It does not say He cannot come in flesh. He appeared to Abraham as a man, and the child of Isaiah 9 is called Mighty God.
defense.askBack: *"Is anything too hard for Yahweh?"*

defense.objection: "No one can die for another's sins. Ezekiel 18."
defense.response: Ezekiel is answering people who blamed their fathers for their own judgment; each sinner answers for his own sin. That is the problem, not the solution. The whole sacrificial system is an innocent substitute bearing guilt, and Isaiah says Yahweh laid our iniquity on the Servant.
defense.askBack: *"Then what was the goat on Yom Kippur doing?"*

defense.objection: "God hates human sacrifice."
defense.response: He forbids men to offer their children to idols. Here it is God who gives, and the Servant who willingly gives himself. Yahweh was pleased to crush him, and he poured out himself to death. No one took his life from him.
defense.askBack: *"Who is the offerer in Isaiah 53:10?"*

defense.objection: "We don't need a sacrifice. We repent."
defense.response: Repentance is commanded, and it is not payment. A judge who lets the guilty go because they are sorry is not just, and God says He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. Someone bears it: you, or the substitute God provided.
defense.askBack: *"If God just overlooks sin, is He still just?"*

defense.objection: "I'm a good person. God weighs the good against the bad."
defense.response: Scripture has no scale like that. It says no one living is righteous before Him and that even our righteous deeds are stained. Use the commandments: see [The Way of the Master](/topic/the-way-of-the-master).
defense.askBack: *"Have you loved God with all your heart every day of your life?"*

defense.objection: "If I believe in Jesus I stop being Jewish."
defense.response: Jesus is Jewish. So were the apostles and the whole first church, thousands in Jerusalem, many of them priests. Paul said, "I too am an Israelite." Following Israel's Messiah is the most Jewish thing a person can do. Do admit the cost: family may treat it as betrayal, and Jesus said He is worth it.
defense.askBack: *"Was Paul still Jewish after the Damascus road?"*

defense.objection: "Christians have persecuted us for centuries."
defense.response: Agree, and grieve it. Crusades, expulsions and pogroms were done in Christ's name against Christ's commands. They were sin. Judge Jesus by Jesus: He wept over Jerusalem and prayed for those who crucified Him.
defense.askBack: *"Would you judge Moses by the Israelites who made the golden calf?"*

defense.objection: "The New Testament is antisemitic."
defense.response: It was written by Jews about a Jewish Messiah, and its hard words to Israel are no harder than Isaiah's or Jeremiah's. It says salvation is from the Jews, that the gospel is for the Jew first, and that God has not rejected His people.
defense.askBack: *"Was Isaiah antisemitic when he called Israel a sinful nation?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus broke the Torah and abolished it."
defense.response: He said He came to fulfill the Law and the Prophets, not abolish them, and no one could convict Him of sin. What He rejected were traditions added to God's word. And God Himself promised a new covenant unlike Sinai.
defense.askBack: *"Which commandment of Moses did Jesus break?"*

defense.objection: "If Jesus were the Messiah, the rabbis would have believed."
defense.response: Isaiah foretold the opposite: "Who has believed our message?" The Servant is despised and rejected by his own. Yet thousands of Jews did believe, including many priests. Paul says a partial hardening has come on Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in, and then all Israel will be saved.
defense.askBack: *"Did Israel's leaders usually listen to the prophets God sent?"*

defense.objection: "Christians say the church has replaced Israel. God is done with us."
defense.response: Scripture does not say so. God tied His promise to Israel to the sun, moon and stars. Within the nation there has always been a believing remnant, and Paul says the day is coming when the nation and the remnant are the same: all Israel will be saved, when they look on the One they pierced [Abner Chou; MacArthur].
defense.askBack: *"Why are there still Jewish people on earth, when the Hittites and Amorites are gone?"*

defense.objection: "I'm Jewish, but I'm not religious."
defense.response: Most Jewish people you meet are here. Don't argue rabbinics. Ask what they think happens after death, use the commandments, and then show them Isaiah 53 as something from their own heritage they may never have seen. See [The Gospel](/topic/the-gospel).
defense.askBack: *"Have you ever read the prophets for yourself?"*

items.text: "Ask a rabbi; he can explain Isaiah 53." (Answer: *"I'd be glad to hear it. Would you read the chapter yourself first and tell me who you see?"*)
"We don't believe in that." (Ask: *"What do you believe God does with sin?"*)
"My family would disown me." (Don't minimize it. Leave Matt 10:37–39 and Ps 27:10, and stay a friend.)
"That's your Bible, not ours." (Stay in Isaiah, Leviticus, Daniel and Zechariah, which are theirs.)

beliefs.text: Hinduism is a family of traditions, not one creed. Common ground: ultimate reality is Brahman, and the true self (atman) is one with it, "You are that" [Chandogya Upanishad 6.8.7]. The many gods are faces of the one reality, and many Hindus are devoted to one of them, such as Vishnu, Shiva or Krishna. Every soul is reborn again and again (samsara), and karma, the moral weight of your deeds, decides the next life. The goal is release (moksha), reached by the path of works, the path of knowledge or the path of devotion. Truth is one and the paths are many, so Jesus is welcome as one more teacher or avatar among others; Krishna says he comes age after age [Bhagavad Gita 4.7–8].

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Who God is, and how guilt is removed. Scripture says God is the personal Creator, distinct from everything He made, who will not share His glory with images. And it says sin is not a weight to be worked off over many lives but guilt before a holy Judge, which only a substitute can bear. John MacArthur puts the line where Scripture does: "all false religion is demon worship" [MacArthur, pastors' session on 2 Corinthians 6]. That is a statement about the system and what stands behind the idol, not an insult to the person in front of you. (Isa 45:5–6; Rom 1:22–25; 1 Cor 10:19–20; Heb 9:27)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"How much karma do you have left to pay, and how would you ever know when it is paid?"* (Col 2:13–14)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth: He is not the world and the world is not He. He says, "I am Yahweh, and there is no other." Idols have mouths and cannot speak. It is appointed for men to die once, and after this comes judgment. And God canceled the record of debt against us by nailing it to the cross. (Gen 1:1; Isa 45:5–6; Ps 115:4–8; Heb 9:27; Col 2:13–14)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"All paths lead to the same God. Truth is one; the wise call it by many names."* → That is itself one path's claim, and it says every path that disagrees is wrong. The paths do not even agree on whether God is personal. Jesus did not offer Himself as one of many: "No one comes to the Father but through Me." If He was wrong, He is not a great teacher. If He was right, the other paths do not arrive. See [The exclusivity of Christ](/topic/the-exclusivity-of-christ). (John 14:6; Acts 4:12; Isa 43:10–11)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"Karma says you get what you deserve. What if someone took what you deserve, once, and gave you what He deserves?"* Christ suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring us to God. Not many lives of paying: one death, one resurrection, and rest. (1 Pet 3:18; Heb 9:26–28; Rom 6:23; Matt 11:28)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: This world is not all there is. Our actions have moral weight, and a man reaps what he sows. Something is wrong with us that we cannot shake. Devotion, discipline, family and reverence matter. Many Hindus are warm, hospitable and glad to talk about God.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: A Hindu will usually agree with everything you say about Jesus and simply add Him to the shelf. So the work is not getting Jesus accepted; it is showing that He will not be added. Don't open by attacking their gods or their food. Ask what they hope for after death and whether they are sure. Then tell them plainly who God is, the Creator who made them, as Paul did with idol-worshipers in Athens and Lystra. Expect family cost to be heavy: baptism can mean losing a family. Be a real friend and open your home. (Acts 17:22–31; Acts 14:15–17; 1 Thess 1:9; Mark 10:29–30)

cheatCard.text: **Heb 9:27**: *"One death, then judgment. If that is true, what happens to the plan of many lives?"*
**Isa 45:5–6**: *"God says there is no other. Can He be one of many?"*
**Ps 115:4–8**: *"Can something a man made hear a man's prayer?"*
**John 14:6**: *"Did Jesus say He was a way, or the way?"*
**Col 2:13–14**: *"What did God do with the record of debt?"*
**Matt 11:28**: *"Who else offers rest instead of more work?"*

altOpeners.text: *"Do you think you are closer to moksha than you were ten years ago? How can you tell?"*

chain.text: **Gal 6:7**: Start with agreement. God is not mocked; whatever a man sows he will also reap. Moral cause and effect is real. *"So what have we sown?"*
**Rom 3:10–12, 23**: There is none righteous, not even one. All have sinned. *"By your own standard, do you add more good karma than bad in a day? In thought as well?"*
**James 2:10**: Whoever keeps the whole law and stumbles in one point is guilty of all. The debt does not shrink with time; every life would add to it.
**Heb 9:27**: It is appointed for men to die once, and after this comes judgment. There is no second lifetime to catch up in. *"If that is true, how much time do you have?"*
**Ps 49:7–8**: No man can redeem his brother or give God a ransom for him. No guru, priest or ritual can carry another man's guilt.

**Col 2:13–14; 1 Pet 3:18**: God canceled the record of debt, nailing it to the cross. Christ suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous. *"Karma is you paying. The gospel is God paying. Which is better news?"*
**Eph 2:8–9**: By grace you have been saved through faith, not of works, so that no one may boast.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Grace is unjust. Everyone must pay for their own deeds."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God agrees that sin must be paid for; He does not wave it away. That is why the cross was necessary. Justice was done there, on a willing substitute. (Rom 3:25–26; Isa 53:5–6)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Suffering is the result of past lives."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Jesus was asked that very question about a man born blind: "Who sinned, this man or his parents?" He said neither. And think what the idea does: it tells the child in the slum that she deserved it. Jesus touched the people karma tells you to leave alone. See [The problem of evil](/topic/the-problem-of-evil). (John 9:1–3; Luke 13:1–5; Matt 8:2–3)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I follow the path of devotion. My god gives grace too."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Ask how the god deals with the guilt. Does anyone pay, or is it just overlooked? Only at the cross is the debt actually settled, by a God who really entered history, died and rose. (Heb 9:22; 1 Cor 15:3–4)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I don't remember past lives, but I trust the teaching."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Why should a person suffer for deeds he cannot remember and so cannot repent of? Scripture has every person answer for the life he actually lived. (2 Cor 5:10; Ezek 18:20)

opener.text: *"What do you believe happens to you when you die?"*

closer.text: *"Jesus said, 'Come to Me, all who are weary and heavy-laden, and I will give you rest.' Every other path says do. He says done. Would you come to Him?"* (Matt 11:28–30; John 19:30)

altOpeners.text: *"If everything is God, is evil God too?"*

chain.text: **Gen 1:1; Acts 17:24–25**: God made the world and everything in it. He does not live in temples made by hands, and is not served by human hands as though He needed anything. He is before and above all He made.
**Isa 44:6; Isa 45:5–6**: "I am the first and I am the last, and there is no God besides Me." *"Can that God be one manifestation among millions?"*
**Ex 20:3–5**: No other gods, and no image to bow to. He is jealous for His people the way a husband is for his wife.
**Ps 115:4–8; Isa 44:16–17**: The idol has eyes and cannot see. A man burns half the log for his supper and bows to the other half. *"Who is greater, the maker or the thing made?"*
**Rom 1:22–25**: Men exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of man, birds, animals and crawling things, and worshiped the creature rather than the Creator.
**1 Cor 10:19–20**: The idol is nothing, but what is sacrificed to it is sacrificed to demons and not to God. The spiritual experiences can be real and still not be from God.

**John 1:1, 14, 18**: The true God has made Himself known, not in thousands of forms, but once, in the Word who became flesh. **Acts 17:30–31**: He now commands all people everywhere to repent, and has given proof by raising Him from the dead.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The images are only aids. We worship the one reality behind them."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Israel said the same of the golden calf: "a feast to Yahweh." God still called it great sin. He decides how He is worshiped. (Ex 32:4–5; Deut 4:15–16; John 4:24)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Jesus is an avatar, like Krishna."*
ifTheySay.youSay: An avatar comes many times and only appears as a man. Jesus became truly man once, died a real death for sins, rose bodily, and said no one comes to the Father except through Him. He leaves no room on the shelf. (Heb 9:26; Luke 24:39; John 14:6)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I am one with God. The self is divine."*
ifTheySay.youSay: That is the oldest lie: "You will be like God." You get tired, you forget, you sin, you die. You are a creature, made in God's image, which is honor enough, and you need a Savior. (Gen 3:5; Isa 31:3; Ps 100:3)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"My religion is far older than yours."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Age is not truth, and the God of the Bible is the Creator before any religion. He was at the beginning. (Gen 1:1; Ps 90:2)

opener.text: *"When you pray, who is listening? Is God a someone, or a something?"*

closer.text: *"You turned to many gods hoping one would hear. There is a living God who made you, sees you and has spoken. People in the first century 'turned to God from idols to serve a living and true God.' Will you?"* (1 Thess 1:9–10; Acts 14:15)

defense.objection: "All religions are paths up the same mountain."
defense.response: The religions disagree about what is at the top: a personal Creator, an impersonal oneness, or nothing. And who is standing high enough to see that all paths meet? Only God has that view, and He has spoken.
defense.askBack: *"How do you know they all arrive?"*

defense.objection: "I already believe in Jesus. He is one of my gods."
defense.response: The Jesus of the Gospels refuses that place. He said to love Him more than father or mother, and that whoever is not with Him is against Him. To honor Him among others is not to believe Him.
defense.askBack: *"What did Jesus say about other ways to the Father?"*

defense.objection: "Christianity is a Western religion."
defense.response: Jesus was born in Asia, and by long tradition the gospel reached India in the first century. Scripture's vision is every tribe, tongue and nation before the throne. Christ is not the West's god; He is the Lord of all.
defense.askBack: *"Was Jesus a Westerner?"*

defense.objection: "Karma explains suffering better than your God does."
defense.response: It explains it by blaming the sufferer, and it offers no one to help. The Bible says the world is fallen through sin, that God Himself entered the suffering, and that He will end it.
defense.askBack: *"What does karma say to a suffering child?"*

defense.objection: "We will be reborn. There is always another chance."
defense.response: Scripture says we die once and then face judgment. And the teaching itself gives no hope: the debt grows each life. Jesus offers not another round but eternal life now.
defense.askBack: *"If there were no next life, would you be ready?"*

defense.objection: "God is in everything and everyone."
defense.response: God is present everywhere, but He is not everything. He made the world and is distinct from it. If all is God, there is no difference between good and evil, and no one to pray to.
defense.askBack: *"Is cruelty also God?"*

defense.objection: "Meditation and yoga give me real peace and real experiences."
defense.response: An experience can be real and not be true. Scripture warns that Satan disguises himself as an angel of light and tells us to test the spirits. Peace with God is not a feeling produced by technique; it is a standing, given through Christ.
defense.askBack: *"Does the peace deal with your guilt, or only quiet it?"*

defense.objection: "Christians are intolerant to say only Jesus saves."
defense.response: We did not make the claim; Jesus did. If a doctor has the one cure, telling you so is love. And we say it as people who needed the cure ourselves.
defense.askBack: *"If it were true, would you want me to tell you?"*

defense.objection: "My family would be dishonored if I became a Christian."
defense.response: Do not make light of it. Jesus said it would cost exactly this, and promised a hundredfold family in His people and eternal life. Then be that family.
defense.askBack: *"What would make Him worth that cost?"*

items.text: "It's all the same in the end." (Ask: *"Did Jesus think so?"* and leave John 14:6.)
"I'll add that to my prayers." (Say gently: *"He asks for all of you, not a place among others. Would you read the Gospel of John?"*)
"This is my culture." (Affirm what is good in it, then: *"The question is what is true."*)
Smiling agreement with everything. (Don't mistake politeness for faith. Ask one direct question: *"Who do you believe Jesus is?"*)

beliefs.text: There is no Creator God to answer to. The Buddha taught Four Noble Truths: life is suffering (dukkha); suffering comes from craving; suffering ends when craving ends; and the way to end it is the Eightfold Path of right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and concentration. There is no permanent self or soul (anatta). Beings are reborn according to karma until they reach nirvana, the "blowing out" of craving and of rebirth. Each person must do it himself: "By oneself is one purified… no one can purify another" [Dhammapada 165]; "You yourselves must strive; the Buddhas only point the way" [Dhammapada 276]. Many Western Buddhists keep the meditation and ethics and hold the rest loosely.
