lead.text: There is no Creator God to answer to. The Buddha taught Four Noble Truths: life is suffering (dukkha); suffering comes from craving; suffering ends when craving ends; and the way to end it is the Eightfold Path of right view, intention, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and concentration. There is no permanent self or soul (anatta). Beings are reborn according to karma until they reach nirvana, the "blowing out" of craving and of rebirth. Each person must do it himself: "By oneself is one purified… no one can purify another" [Dhammapada 165]; "You yourselves must strive; the Buddhas only point the way" [Dhammapada 276]. Many Western Buddhists keep the meditation and ethics and hold the rest loosely.

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: What is wrong with us, and who can fix it. Buddhism says the problem is desire and the cure is to put it out by your own effort. Scripture says the problem is sin against a holy God, that we cannot cure ourselves, and that God has provided a Savior. Buddhism has a path and no one to forgive you. (Rom 3:23; Jer 17:9; Rom 5:6–8; Acts 4:12)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"When you do something wrong, who forgives you?"* (Ps 51:4)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: In the beginning God created, so there is Someone we answer to. He made man in His image, a real person who matters. Suffering came in through sin, and it is not an illusion to rise above: Jesus wept at a grave. The answer to desire is not to put it out but to have it filled: in God's presence is fullness of joy. And one day He will wipe away every tear. (Gen 1:1; Gen 1:27; Rom 5:12; John 11:35; Ps 16:11; Rev 21:4)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"Buddhism isn't a religion. It's just a practice for peace of mind."* → Then it has nothing to say about your guilt, your death or your Maker, and those are the questions that matter most. A calm mind on the way to judgment is not safety. Jesus gives peace with God first, and then the peace of God. (Heb 9:27; Rom 5:1; John 14:27; Phil 4:6–7)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"The Buddha said, 'Strive.' His last words were to keep working at it. Jesus' last words on the cross were, 'It is finished.' Which do you need?"* Jesus said, "I am the way." He does not point to the path; He is the path, and He carries those who cannot walk it. (John 19:30; John 14:6; Matt 11:28–30; Eph 2:8–9)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: Life in this world is marked by suffering, and nothing here lasts. Craving for things that cannot satisfy does make us miserable; Scripture says the same about covetousness and the love of the world. Compassion, self-control, honesty and a quiet mind are good. Death must be faced, not ignored.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: Most Buddhists you will meet in America are either from Buddhist families (Thai, Vietnamese, Japanese, Chinese and others) or Westerners who came for meditation. Ask which, and ask what they actually believe; many have never thought about a Creator. Start with the Creator, as Paul did with people who had no Bible, and then the conscience. Honor their seriousness about suffering and show them the One who entered it. Don't mock the Buddha; he is dead and never claimed to save anyone. The contrast with a living Savior makes itself. (Acts 17:24–31; Rom 2:14–15; Heb 4:15; 1 Pet 3:15)

**Ps 51:4**: *"When you do wrong, who is wronged, and who can forgive it?"*
**Ps 16:11**: *"What if the answer to desire is not less of it, but the right object?"*
**John 11:25–26**: *"The Buddha is in his grave. What did Jesus say at one?"*
**John 19:30**: *"'Strive on,' or 'It is finished'?"*
**Rev 21:4**: *"Who can promise an end to suffering and has the power to do it?"*

offense.title: Who forgives you?
offense.subtitle: the problem is sin, not desire

altOpeners.text: *"Have you ever done something you knew was wrong? What did you do with the guilt?"*

chain.text: **Rom 2:14–15**: Everyone has a conscience that accuses him. Buddhism has its own precepts: no killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying or intoxication. *"Have you kept even those?"*
**Ps 51:4**: "Against You, You only, I have sinned." Wrong is not just unskillful; it is personal. It is against Someone. *"If there is no God, why does guilt feel like owing someone?"*
**Jer 17:9; Mark 7:21–23**: The trouble is not that we desire, but that the heart is corrupt. Evil comes from within.
**Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23**: All have sinned, and the wages of sin is death. Not rebirth: death and judgment. (Heb 9:27)
**Rom 5:6–8**: While we were still helpless, Christ died for the ungodly. *"The path says purify yourself. What if you can't?"*
**Ps 103:10–12**: He has not dealt with us according to our sins. As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us. *"Does karma ever say that?"*
**1 John 1:9**: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous to forgive. Forgiveness needs a Person. Buddhism has none to give it.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"There is no sin, only ignorance and unskillful action."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Then no one has ever truly been wronged, and no cruelty is truly evil. You don't live as if that were so. Jeff Durbin's observation to a skeptic applies: when you speak of compassion and human worth, you are borrowing from a world God made. (Rom 1:19–20; Rom 2:15)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"There is no self, so there is no one to be guilty."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Then there is no one to be compassionate to, and no one to reach nirvana. You love real people. Scripture explains why: each is made in God's image. (Gen 1:27; Ps 139:13–14)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I make merit to balance it."*
ifTheySay.youSay: How much is enough, and who keeps the account? Our best deeds are stained. A gift cannot be earned. (Isa 64:6; Titus 3:5; Eph 2:8–9)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Amida Buddha saves by grace."* (Pure Land)
ifTheySay.youSay: You are right to see that we cannot save ourselves. But grace needs a real Savior who actually dealt with sin in history. Jesus lived, died under Pontius Pilate and rose; witnesses saw Him. (1 Cor 15:3–8; Acts 4:12)

opener.text: *"What do you think is the deepest problem with people?"*

closer.text: *"The Buddha could point to a path. He could not forgive one sin. Jesus said to a paralyzed man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' and proved He had the authority. Would you bring yours to Him?"* (Mark 2:5–12; Matt 11:28)

altOpeners.text: *"Is the goal to stop wanting, or to finally have what you were made for?"*

chain.text: **Gen 1:31; Gen 3:17–19**: God made the world very good. Suffering is not the nature of existence; it is an intruder that came with sin. That is why it feels wrong.
**Eccl 3:11**: God has set eternity in man's heart. Our longing is not the disease; it is a clue. We were made for Someone.
**Jer 2:13**: "They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, to hew for themselves broken cisterns that can hold no water." The problem is desire aimed at the wrong things.
**John 4:13–14; John 6:35**: Jesus does not say "stop thirsting." He says, "Whoever drinks of the water that I will give him shall never thirst."
**John 11:25–26, 35**: At a friend's grave Jesus wept, and then said, "I am the resurrection and the life." He does not detach from suffering; He enters it and defeats it.
**1 Cor 15:20, 54–57**: Christ has been raised. Death is swallowed up in victory. The hope is not that the candle goes out, but that the dead are raised.
**Rev 21:3–5**: God will dwell with His people and wipe away every tear; no more death, mourning or pain. "Behold, I am making all things new."

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Attachment is the cause of suffering, so the wise love without attachment."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God so loved the world that He gave His Son. Love that costs nothing is not love. The Bible's answer to loss is not caring less, but a resurrection in which nothing given to God is lost. (John 3:16; John 15:13; 1 Thess 4:13–14)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Everything is impermanent."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Everything created, yes. "The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever." There is One who does not change. (Isa 40:8; Mal 3:6; Heb 13:8)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Meditation has ended a lot of my suffering."*
ifTheySay.youSay: It may have quieted your mind. It has not dealt with death, guilt or God. Jesus offers rest for the soul and a peace the world cannot give. (Matt 11:28–29; John 14:27)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Buddha was enlightened. Why not follow both?"*
ifTheySay.youSay: They point opposite ways: no God or the living God; no self or an eternal soul; escape or resurrection. And only one of them rose from the dead. See [The resurrection](/topic/the-resurrection).

opener.text: *"What is nirvana like? Is there a 'you' there to enjoy it?"*

closer.text: *"You have been honest that life hurts. Jesus is the only one who says He will end the hurt without ending you. 'I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly.' Would you look at Him?"* (John 10:10; Rev 21:4)

defense.objection: "Buddhism is a philosophy, not a religion. It fits with any belief."
defense.response: The Buddha's teaching has no Creator and no soul. Jesus teaches both, and says He is the only way. They cannot both be right.
defense.askBack: *"Which of the two would you give up?"*

defense.objection: "There is no creator. The universe has always cycled."
defense.response: Something that changes and decays cannot be eternal and self-explaining. Creation shows God's eternal power so plainly that men are without excuse. See [Worldviews: how do you know?](/topic/worldviews-how-do-you-know).
defense.askBack: *"Why is there something and not nothing?"*

defense.objection: "Desire is the root of suffering."
defense.response: Wrong desire is. God made us to desire, and commands us to delight in Him. Sin is what brought suffering in.
defense.askBack: *"Is the desire to end suffering also a problem?"*

defense.objection: "There is no self."
defense.response: Then who is practicing, and who is reborn? You know you are someone. God made you in His image and knows you by name.
defense.askBack: *"Who is the one asking?"*

defense.objection: "I'm responsible for my own liberation."
defense.response: That is honest, and it is the bad news. No one keeps the path perfectly. The gospel is for the helpless.
defense.askBack: *"How is the path going?"*

defense.objection: "Karma is perfectly fair."
defense.response: Fair is exactly what we should fear. And with no judge, who administers it? Scripture has a Judge who is just, and who also made a way for mercy.
defense.askBack: *"Do you want what you deserve?"*

defense.objection: "Christians believe in hell. Buddhism is more compassionate."
defense.response: Traditional Buddhism has hells too, for ages. The question is what is true. The same Jesus who warned of hell died to keep people out of it. See [Hell and eternal judgment](/topic/hell-and-eternal-judgment).
defense.askBack: *"If the warning is true, is it unkind to give it?"*

defense.objection: "All teachers say the same thing: be kind."
defense.response: They share some ethics and differ on everything underneath. Only Jesus claimed to be God, died for sins and rose. Kindness does not remove guilt.
defense.askBack: *"Did the Buddha claim to forgive sins?"*

defense.objection: "I just live in the present moment."
defense.response: Good, as far as it goes. But the present moment is moving toward a day God has fixed. Wisdom numbers its days.
defense.askBack: *"What happens in the moment after your last one?"*

items.text: "It works for me." (Ask: *"Does it work for your guilt and your death?"*)
"I don't think in terms of God." (Leave Gen 1:1 and the question, *"What if there is One who thinks in terms of you?"*)
"Let's not be attached to views." (Smile: *"That is a view. Jesus made claims. Would you read Mark and weigh them?"*)
Calm agreement and a change of subject. (Leave one sentence: *"Strive on," or "It is finished."*)

beliefs.text: There is no book and no creed, which is the point: "I'm spiritual, not religious." The common threads are these. All is one, and the divine is an energy or consciousness in everything, often called "the Universe." You are divine at your core, and your problem is not sin but forgetting who you are. You create your own reality by your thoughts (manifestation, the law of attraction). Truth is personal: "my truth." Guidance comes from within, and from tools such as astrology, tarot, crystals, energy healing, psychedelics, spirit guides, angels and the dead. Most believe in reincarnation and karma. Jesus is an enlightened teacher who reached "Christ consciousness," which anyone can reach.

Jesus is an enlightened teacher who reached "Christ consciousness," which anyone can reach.

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Who is God: the Creator, or you. Scripture draws a hard line between the Creator and everything He made, says the human heart is not divine but deceitful, and calls contact with spirits what it is. The first lie in the Bible is the New Age gospel in five words: "You will be like God." (Gen 3:4–5; Rom 1:25; Jer 17:9; Isa 45:5)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"If your truth and my truth contradict each other, can they both be true? And how do you know the voice you are listening to is good?"* (1 John 4:1)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: God made the world; He is not the world, and neither are you. He forbids divination, fortune-telling, mediums and calling up the dead, because they are detestable to Him and because He has spoken. Satan disguises himself as an angel of light. There is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. It is appointed for men to die once, and after this comes judgment. (Acts 17:24–25; Deut 18:10–12; Isa 8:19–20; 2 Cor 11:14; 1 Tim 2:5; Heb 9:27)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"I've had real experiences. I've felt the energy, and my readings come true."* → I believe you. The Bible never says these things are fake; it says they are forbidden. A slave girl in Philippi told fortunes accurately by a spirit, and Paul cast it out. Real is not the same as good. The test of a spirit is what it says about Jesus. (Acts 16:16–18; 1 John 4:1–3; Deut 13:1–3)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"You have been told to look within. What if what is within is the problem, and the help has to come from outside you?"* You are not God, and that is good news: you don't have to hold your universe together. The God who made you came for you. He does not ask you to raise your vibration; He raises the dead. (Mark 7:21–23; Eph 2:4–5; Col 1:16–17; John 10:10)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: There is more to reality than matter. The spiritual world is real. People are more than animals, the world's religion of money and status is empty, and a great deal of church life has been cold and hypocritical. We are made for something beyond ourselves.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: This is probably the most common belief you will meet, often mixed with a church background. Many came to it through pain, illness or a bad church. Ask what they practice and what they were looking for when they started. Don't mock crystals; go to the heart: who is God, what is wrong with us, how do you know. Define every word, because they will say "Christ," "light," "spirit" and "energy" with other meanings. Take the spirits seriously, not fearfully: greater is He who is in you. Expect "that's your truth"; answer it once, kindly, and go back to Jesus. MacArthur's warning about the pull of false religion applies here in full, and he includes every system in it. (Col 2:8; 1 John 4:4; Acts 19:18–20; Jude 1:22–23)

cheatCard.text: **Gen 3:4–5**: *"Who first said, 'You will be like God'?"*
**Jer 17:9**: *"If the heart is deceitful, is 'follow your heart' safe advice?"*
**Deut 18:10–12**: *"What does God say about mediums, fortune-telling and divination?"*
**2 Cor 11:14**: *"If a spirit of darkness came to you, how would it look?"*
**John 14:6**: *"Did Jesus say 'find your truth,' or 'I am the truth'?"*
**Heb 9:27**: *"How many times does a person die?"*

altOpeners.text: *"If we are all divine, why is the world like this?"*

chain.text: **Gen 1:1; Acts 17:24–25**: God made the world and everything in it, and gives to all people life and breath. He is the giver; we are the receivers. *"Did you make yourself?"*
**Isa 45:5; Isa 46:9**: "I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is no one like Me." That leaves no room for seven billion more.
**Gen 3:4–5**: The serpent's offer was, "You will be like God." *"The idea that we are divine is not new. Where did it first come from, and how did it turn out?"*
**Ezek 28:2**: "You are a man and not God, although you make your heart like the heart of God." We get tired, we get sick, we cannot keep our own resolutions, and we die.

**Rom 1:21–25**: Knowing God, men did not honor Him or give thanks, and exchanged the truth of God for a lie, worshiping the creature rather than the Creator. *"Is it possible that 'the Universe' is a way to have spirituality without Someone to answer to?"*
**Mark 7:21–23; Jer 17:9**: What is within is not a spark of God. Jesus said evil comes from within. That is why "look within" cannot save.
**Col 1:16–17; John 1:1–3, 14**: The One through whom all things were made, and in whom all things hold together, became flesh and came to us. *"You don't have to become God. God became man."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Jesus said, 'The kingdom of God is within you.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: He said it to Pharisees who were plotting against Him; He was not telling them they were divine. The King was standing in their midst. The same Jesus said that what comes from within a man defiles him. (Luke 17:20–21; Mark 7:20–23)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Jesus reached Christ consciousness, and so can we."*
ifTheySay.youSay: "Christ" is not a state of mind; it is a title, the Messiah, and it belongs to one Man. He warned that many would come saying "I am the Christ." (Matt 16:16; Matt 24:4–5, 23–24; 1 John 2:22)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"We're all children of God."*
ifTheySay.youSay: All are made by God. But the right to become children of God is given to those who receive Christ and believe in His name. (John 1:12; Gal 3:26; Acts 17:28–29)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That's your truth."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Is that statement true for both of us, or only for you? And follow it through: if truth and right are personal, the rapist has his truth too, and no one can say he was wrong. You don't believe that. Some things are wrong for everyone, which means there is a standard above all of us. Jesus did not say He had a truth. He said, "I am the truth." See [Faith and reason](/topic/faith-and-reason). (John 14:6; John 18:37)

opener.text: *"When you say 'the Universe,' do you mean a someone or a something? Does it know your name?"*

closer.text: *"Being your own god is exhausting. You were never meant to hold it all together. There is One who does, and He says, 'Come to Me.' Would you?"* (Col 1:17; Matt 11:28)

altOpeners.text: *"Has anything you've encountered ever frightened you?"*

chain.text: **Eph 6:12; 1 Pet 5:8**: The Bible agrees the spirit world is real, and says not all of it is friendly. There are spiritual forces of wickedness, and an adversary who prowls like a lion.
**2 Cor 11:14**: Satan disguises himself as an angel of light. A deceiving spirit would be warm, wise-sounding and affirming. *"So how would you tell?"*

**Deut 18:10–12**: God forbids divination, omens, sorcery, mediums, spiritists and calling up the dead, and calls them detestable. That covers tarot, astrology, channeling and séances. **Isa 47:13–14**: the stargazers cannot even save themselves.
**Isa 8:19–20**: "Should not a people consult their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living? To the law and to the testimony!" God is not silent; He has spoken in His word.
**1 John 4:1–3**: Test the spirits. Every spirit that does not confess Jesus, the Christ come in the flesh, is not from God. *"What do your guides say about Jesus dying for sins?"*
**1 Tim 2:5; Heb 4:14–16**: There is one mediator. You do not need a psychic, a guide or a dead relative; you may come straight to the throne of grace through Christ.

**Acts 19:18–20; Col 2:15**: In Ephesus those who had practiced magic brought their books and burned them. Christ disarmed the rulers and authorities at the cross. *"Whatever you have opened the door to, He is stronger."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"My guides are loving. They only tell me good things."*
ifTheySay.youSay: A spirit that never names your sin and never points you to Christ's cross is telling you what the serpent told Eve: you will not die. Love tells the truth. (Gen 3:4; Jer 6:14; Gal 1:8)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I talk to my grandmother. It comforts me."*
ifTheySay.youSay: I'm sorry for your loss. Scripture says the dead do not return to guide us, and forbids seeking them, so whatever is answering is not her. The God of all comfort invites you to bring that grief to Him. (Luke 16:26; Deut 18:11; 2 Cor 1:3–4)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"It's just for fun. Astrology is harmless."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God does not call it harmless, and it trains you to look to creation for what only the Creator gives. He made the stars; ask Him. (Deut 4:19; Isa 47:13; James 1:5)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Christians are afraid of everything."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Not afraid: free. "Greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." We simply don't go where our Father said not to. (1 John 4:4; 2 Tim 1:7)

opener.text: *"How do you know that your guides, or the cards, are telling you the truth?"*

closer.text: *"You've been looking for a voice you can trust. There is one who proved He can be trusted by dying for you and walking out of His grave. 'My sheep hear My voice.' Would you listen to Him in the Gospel of John?"* (John 10:27–28; John 20:31)

defense.objection: "I'm spiritual, not religious."
defense.response: Jesus was hard on empty religion too. But "spiritual" still has to answer: which spirit, and is it true? The alternative to dead religion is not making it up; it is knowing the living God.
defense.askBack: *"What does 'spiritual' mean to you?"*

defense.objection: "The Universe has my back."
defense.response: An impersonal universe cannot love, hear or keep a promise. What you are hoping for is a Father. There is one, and He has a name.
defense.askBack: *"Has the Universe ever forgiven you?"*

defense.objection: "I manifest my reality. Thoughts become things."
defense.response: Then every suffering person caused their own cancer, and you carry a weight no one can bear. Scripture says God rules and we ask: "If the Lord wills." That is freedom, not control.
defense.askBack: *"Did the child in the hospital manifest that?"*

defense.objection: "We are all one. Separation is an illusion."
defense.response: If all is one, there is no real difference between love and cruelty. The Bible says the separation that matters is real: our sins have separated us from God. And it can be healed.
defense.askBack: *"Is evil part of the oneness?"*

defense.objection: "Right and wrong are personal. Everyone has their own truth."
defense.response: Then no one is ever wrong. The rapist was living his truth. And if you say society decides instead, then what Hitler's Germany did to the Jews was good for them at the time. You know both are false, so there is a standard above every person and every nation. See [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice).
defense.askBack: *"Was that wrong for everyone, or just not your preference?"*

defense.objection: "There's no sin, only lower vibrations and lessons."
defense.response: You don't believe that when you are betrayed. Wrong is real, guilt is real, and renaming it does not remove it. Blood does.
defense.askBack: *"Have you ever needed to be forgiven?"*

defense.objection: "I've lived many lives."
defense.response: Scripture says once, then judgment. And notice that past-life "memories" are always of someone interesting. More to the point: if many lives haven't fixed us, another won't.
defense.askBack: *"If this is the only one, are you ready?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was a great spiritual teacher, like the others."
defense.response: Great teachers don't claim to be God, forgive sins and say all will be judged by them, unless it is true. He is not on the list; He is in a category of one.
defense.askBack: *"Have you read what He actually claimed?"*

defense.objection: "The church suppressed the real, mystical Jesus."
defense.response: The "hidden" gospels are second-century and later, and read nothing like eyewitness accounts. The four Gospels come from the first century and the apostles' circle. See [Is the Bible reliable?](/topic/is-the-bible-reliable).
defense.askBack: *"Which source is closest to the events?"*

defense.objection: "Crystals, sage and energy work heal me."
defense.response: God made stones and plants good, and they are not gods. To look to created things for protection and power is the exchange Romans 1 describes. Bring the need to the One who made them.
defense.askBack: *"What is it you are hoping to be healed of?"*

defense.objection: "Everything happens for a reason, and it all works out for everyone."
defense.response: God does rule all things, and He promises good to those who love Him and are called by Him. For those who refuse Him, Scripture promises judgment. Don't take the comfort without the Christ.
defense.askBack: *"Whose reason? Who is behind it?"*

items.text: "That's your truth." (Ask: *"Is that true for me too?"* and leave John 14:6.)
"You're giving off negative energy." (Smile: *"I may be. I'd rather be honest with you than agreeable."*)
"I respect all paths." (Ask: *"Including the one that says there is only one?"*)
"I'll see what my guides say." (Give 1 John 4:1–3 and ask them to put that test to the guide.)

beliefs.text: There are three kinds, and you need to know which one is in front of you. Most are atheists: the Church of Satan (Anton LaVey, 1966) does not believe in a real devil and uses Satan as a symbol of pride, appetite and being your own god; its first statement is "Satan represents indulgence instead of abstinence!" [LaVey, The Satanic Bible, 1969]. The Satanic Temple (2013) is also non-theistic and is mainly a political and activist group with seven tenets about reason, empathy and bodily autonomy, such as "One's body is inviolable, subject to one's own will alone" [The Satanic Temple, Tenet III]. A small minority are theistic: they believe Satan or Lucifer is a real being and honor or worship him, often mixed with occult practice. What all three share is the creed of the garden: no God over me; I decide good and evil.

[LaVey, The Satanic Bible, 1969]. The Satanic Temple (2013) is also non-theistic and is mainly a political and activist group with seven tenets about reason, empathy and bodily autonomy, such as "One's body is inviolable, subject to one's own will alone" [The Satanic Temple, Tenet III]. A small minority are theistic: they believe Satan or Lucifer is a real being and honor or worship him, often mixed with occult practice. What all three share is the creed of the garden: no God over me; I decide good and evil.

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Who is God: the Creator, or the self. Satanism in every form is the worship of self, which is exactly what Scripture says the devil offered at the start and still offers. And Scripture says the devil is real whether a man believes in him or not: a created, fallen, lying, defeated enemy who has never loved anyone who served him. (Gen 3:4–5; Isa 14:13–14; John 8:44; Rom 1:25)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"Jesus said everyone who sins is a slave of sin. Has doing whatever you want made you free, or does it own you?"* (John 8:34)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: Satan said in his heart, "I will make myself like the Most High," and was cast down. He is a liar and a murderer from the beginning, and he blinds the minds of the unbelieving. The Son of God appeared to destroy the works of the devil, disarmed the rulers and authorities at the cross, and through death rendered powerless him who had the power of death. The devil's end is the lake of fire, and it is shared by those who follow him. (Isa 14:12–15; John 8:44; 2 Cor 4:4; 1 John 3:8; Col 2:15; Heb 2:14–15; Rev 20:10; Matt 25:41)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"I don't believe in Satan or God. It's a symbol, a protest against religious hypocrisy and control."* → Then look at what you chose for a symbol: the first rebel, whose whole message was "be your own god." Scripture says a person does not have to believe in the devil to follow him; he only has to live for himself. All of us once walked that way. And hypocrisy is a reason to reject hypocrites, not Christ, who condemned them harder than you do. (Eph 2:1–3; 2 Cor 4:4; Matt 23:27–28)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"The devil has never died for anyone. Christ did. Which master has actually loved you?"* God rescues people from the domain of darkness and transfers them to the kingdom of His beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins. No one has gone too far: people who practiced magic burned their books and believed. (Col 1:13–14; John 10:10–11; Acts 26:18; Acts 19:18–20; 1 Tim 1:15)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: Religious hypocrisy and abuse are real and should be exposed. No one can be forced into faith; coerced religion is worthless. The individual matters, and honesty is better than pretending. Many of these people were truly wronged by someone who claimed Christ's name.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: Do not be afraid and do not be shocked. Shock is often the point; meet it with calm and kindness. Greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world. Ask which kind they are and how they got there, because there is very often a story of church hurt, abuse or rejection behind it, and you should listen to it. With the atheist kinds, use this page's first play together with the [Atheist](/atheist) plays and [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice): they are atheists in costume. With the theistic and occult kind, take the danger seriously and keep to the gospel. We do not use rituals or formulas of deliverance, and we do not rail at the devil; even Michael the archangel said only, "The Lord rebuke you." Christ sets captives free through His word. Pray before, during and after: see [How to pray](/topic/how-to-pray). (1 John 4:4; 2 Tim 1:7; Jude 1:9; Eph 6:10–12; James 4:7)

**John 8:34**: *"Is doing what you want freedom, or slavery?"*
**John 8:44**: *"What does Jesus say the devil is, from the beginning?"*
**Col 2:15**: *"What happened to the powers of darkness at the cross?"*
**Rev 20:10**: *"How does the devil's story end?"*
**Col 1:13–14**: *"What does God do for those in the domain of darkness?"*

offense.title: Your own god?
offense.subtitle: the atheist kinds: Church of Satan, Satanic Temple

altOpeners.text: *"If you are your own highest authority, who do you answer to when you are wrong?"*

chain.text: **Gen 3:4–5**: The serpent's promise: you will not die, and you will be like God, deciding good and evil for yourself. *"That is the idea you've taken up. It is the oldest one there is. What did it deliver?"* Shame, blame, hiding and death. (Gen 3:7–10)
**Isa 14:13–15**: Five times: "I will." "I will make myself like the Most High." And the answer: "You will be thrust down to Sheol." Self-exaltation is the devil's own biography, and it ends in ruin.
A god should be able to do three things: make himself, keep himself alive and clear his own guilt. *"Which of those can you do?"* (Ps 100:3; Ps 49:7–9)
**John 8:34; Rom 6:16**: Everyone who commits sin is the slave of sin. You are slaves of the one you obey. Indulgence does not end in freedom; ask anyone owned by a bottle, a screen or his own anger.
**Rom 1:21–25**: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie and worshiped the creature rather than the Creator. The self is a creature too.

**Phil 2:5–11**: Set the two side by side. Satan grasped at being God and was cast down. Christ, who is God, emptied Himself, took the form of a slave, obeyed to death on a cross, and was exalted above every name. *"Which one is actually strong?"*
**Matt 16:25–26**: Whoever wants to save his life will lose it. What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Christianity is for the weak. It's a slave religion."*
ifTheySay.youSay: It is for the guilty, which is everyone. As for weak: its founder went to a Roman cross on purpose, forgave the men nailing Him there and walked out of His grave. Self-indulgence takes no strength at all; any child can do it. (John 10:17–18; Luke 23:34; Titus 2:11–12)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Our tenets are more moral than your Bible: compassion, reason, justice."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Those are good things, and they are borrowed. In a world with no God, why is compassion binding on anyone, and why is justice more than opinion? If each person decides, the rapist is never wrong. See [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice). (Rom 2:14–15; Mic 6:8)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I don't hurt anyone. I just live for myself."*
ifTheySay.youSay: The first and greatest commandment is to love God with all your heart, and living for yourself breaks it every hour. And you have hurt people; all of us have. (Matt 22:37–38; Rom 3:23)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"My body is mine alone."*
ifTheySay.youSay: You did not make it and you cannot keep it. It is on loan from the One who knit it together, and He will ask for an account. (Ps 139:13–14; 1 Cor 6:19–20; Heb 9:27)

opener.text: *"What does Satan stand for, to you?"*

closer.text: *"You wanted no master. Everyone has one. Jesus says, 'If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.' Would you like to be?"* (John 8:36; Matt 11:28–30)

offense.title: The real Satan
offense.subtitle: for those who honor him, and for the occult

altOpeners.text: *"Do you know how the Bible says his story ends?"*

chain.text: **Ezek 28:15; Col 1:16**: He is a creature. He was made, and he is not God's opposite or equal. There is no contest between the Creator and something He made.
**Job 1:12; Luke 22:31**: He has to ask permission. He could not touch Job or sift Peter without God's leave. *"Why serve the one on the leash rather than the One holding it?"*
**John 8:44**: Jesus says he was a murderer from the beginning and there is no truth in him; when he lies he speaks his own language. Whatever he has promised you, he is lying.
**2 Cor 11:14; Rev 12:10**: He disguises himself as an angel of light, and he is the accuser. First he flatters, then he accuses. He has no love for those he uses.
**1 Pet 5:8**: He prowls like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. You are not his partner. You are his prey.

**Col 2:15; Heb 2:14–15**: At the cross Christ disarmed the rulers and authorities and made a public display of them. Through death He rendered powerless the one who had the power of death, and freed those enslaved by the fear of it.

**Rev 20:10; Matt 25:41**: The devil will be thrown into the lake of fire, and the eternal fire prepared for him and his angels is where those on his side are sent with him. *"He cannot save himself. He will not save you."*

**Col 1:13–14; Acts 26:18**: God rescues from the domain of darkness and transfers into the kingdom of His Son. Jesus sent Paul to turn people from the authority of Satan to God, to receive forgiveness of sins.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He gives me power. It works."*
ifTheySay.youSay: He offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world for one act of worship. He pays in things that cannot be kept, and the price is you. A girl in Philippi had real power from a spirit, and she was a slave. (Matt 4:8–10; Mark 8:36; Acts 16:16–18)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Lucifer is the light-bringer who freed us with knowledge. God is the tyrant."*
ifTheySay.youSay: He promised they would be like God and would not die. They got shame, fear and a grave. Then look at who the "tyrant" turned out to be: the One who laid down His life for His enemies. The thief comes to steal, kill and destroy; the Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep. (Gen 3:4–10; John 10:10–11; Rom 5:8)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I've gone too far. I gave myself to him."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Your soul was never yours to sign away: "All souls are Mine," God says. Jesus freed a man who had a legion of demons, and saved the man who called himself the foremost of sinners. No pact outranks His blood. (Ezek 18:4; Mark 5:15; 1 Tim 1:15; Col 2:14–15)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I'm afraid of what happens if I leave."*
ifTheySay.youSay: No one can snatch Christ's sheep out of His hand. Submit to God, resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Get rid of the objects and books, as the Ephesians did, and get into a faithful church. (John 10:28–29; James 4:7; Acts 19:18–20)

opener.text: *"What do you believe Satan is, and what has he done for you?"*

closer.text: *"You have served a master who hates you and is already beaten. There is a King who died for His enemies and lives. Will you come over to Him today?"* (Col 1:13–14; John 6:37)

defense.objection: "We don't worship the devil. Satanism is atheism."
defense.response: Understood, and most do mean that. Then the questions are the atheist's: where do reason, worth and right and wrong come from? See the [Atheist](/atheist) plays. And notice what you took for a mascot.
defense.askBack: *"Of all symbols, why that one?"*

defense.objection: "Christians invented lies about us. The Satanic Panic."
defense.response: False accusation is sin, and where Christians spread stories that were not true, they broke the ninth commandment. That does not make the philosophy true. Judge it by what it teaches.
defense.askBack: *"Setting the rumors aside, is 'be your own god' true?"*

defense.objection: "In the Bible, God kills millions and Satan kills a handful."
defense.response: The Giver of life has the right to take it, and every death He decrees is just. The devil is called a murderer from the beginning because he brought death on the whole race with a lie. And only One of them died to give life back.
defense.askBack: *"Who brought death into the world in Genesis 3?"*

defense.objection: "Religion is slavery. I bow to no one."
defense.response: Everyone serves something: appetite, approval, anger, self. The question is which master is good. Christ's yoke is easy, and He calls His servants friends.
defense.askBack: *"What can you not say no to?"*

defense.objection: "We fight for freedom and against theocracy."
defense.response: Faith cannot be forced, and Christians should say so first. But freedom from God is not freedom; it is the far country, and it ends at the pig trough. The Father is still watching the road.
defense.askBack: *"Free for what?"*

defense.objection: "I renounced my baptism."
defense.response: Water never saved anyone, so there was nothing magic to undo. What matters is not a ceremony but Christ, and He receives those who come to Him, including those who once cursed Him.
defense.askBack: *"What would it take for you to come back?"*

defense.objection: "Blasphemy is funny. Hail Satan."
defense.response: God is not shaken; He who sits in the heavens laughs. But ask why it is always Jesus' name and never Zeus's. People do not rage at what they think is nothing. His patience with you is kindness, meant to lead you to repentance.
defense.askBack: *"Why does He bother you so much?"*

defense.objection: "Hell is a threat to control people."
defense.response: Jesus, who warned of it most, is the one who died to keep people out of it. A warning from someone who paid your way out is not a threat. See [Hell and eternal judgment](/topic/hell-and-eternal-judgment).
defense.askBack: *"If it is real, would you want to be told?"*

defense.objection: "I've seen things. Spirits are real, and they answer me."
defense.response: I believe you. Scripture says they are real, that they lie, and that God forbids contact with them because they destroy. Test them by what they say about Jesus.
defense.askBack: *"What do they say about the cross?"*

items.text: "Hail Satan." (Don't flinch. Say: *"He won't hail you back. Jesus would have you."*)
"You're just scared of us." (Smile: *"No. I'm concerned for you. There's a difference."*)
"I had enough of church growing up." (Ask what happened, and listen all the way through.)
"It's just a joke." (Leave John 8:34 and the question, *"Are you free?"*)

beliefs.text: There is one God, and He is one person. Father, Son and Holy Spirit are not three persons but three ways the one God has shown Himself, and His name is Jesus. In their words: "There is one God, who has revealed Himself as our Father, in His Son Jesus Christ, and as the Holy Spirit" [UPCI, Our Beliefs]. Many say "the Son" means the human nature of Christ, which began at Bethlehem, and "the Father" means the deity in Him. Full salvation is "repentance, baptism in water by immersion in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and the baptism of the Holy Ghost with the initial sign of speaking with other tongues" [UPCI, Fundamental Doctrine].

In their words: "There is one God, who has revealed Himself as our Father, in His Son Jesus Christ, and as the Holy Spirit" [UPCI, Our Beliefs]. Many say "the Son" means the human nature of Christ, which began at Bethlehem, and "the Father" means the deity in Him. Full salvation is "repentance, baptism in water by immersion in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and the baptism of the Holy Ghost with the initial sign of speaking with other tongues" [UPCI, Fundamental Doctrine].

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Two things. First, who God is: Scripture shows the Father, the Son and the Spirit loving, sending and speaking to one another, which one person playing three parts cannot do. Second, how a sinner is saved: they add a baptismal formula and tongues to faith in Christ. (John 17:5; Matt 3:16–17; Eph 2:8–9)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"When Jesus prayed, 'Father, glorify Me with the glory I had with You before the world was,' who was He talking to, and when did He have that glory?"* (John 17:5)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: At Jesus' baptism the Son is in the water, the Spirit descends, and the Father speaks from heaven. The Word was **with** God and **was** God. The Father sent the Son, and the Son sends another Helper. The Trinity is what you get when you believe all of it: one God, three persons. (Matt 3:16–17; John 1:1–2; John 14:16–17; Gal 4:4–6; 2 Cor 13:14)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"'Hear, O Israel, Yahweh is one.' You believe in three gods."* → We confess that verse with you. One God, one Being. The question is whether the one God is one person or three, and that has to come from the rest of Scripture, where the Father and the Son speak to and love each other. (Deut 6:4; John 17:24; John 8:17–18)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"If you died tonight, what would you be counting on: Christ's finished work, or that you were baptized with the right words and spoke in tongues?"* The Son the Father sent did everything needed. A sinner is declared right by faith in Him alone. (Rom 4:4–5; John 3:16; Acts 16:31)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: There is one God. Jesus Christ is fully God and fully man, born of a virgin, crucified, bodily risen and coming again. The Bible is God's word. They take holiness seriously and are often zealous and sincere.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: They love the name of Jesus, so start there with warmth. They have usually been taught that the Trinity means three gods, so say plainly what you believe first: one Being, three persons, "one what and three who's." Then stay in John's Gospel and let Jesus' own words about His Father carry it. James White, *The Forgotten Trinity*, ch. 11, is the best short treatment. Don't mock tongues or their standards of dress; keep to who God is and what saves. See [The Trinity](/topic/the-trinity).

cheatCard.text: **John 17:5**: *"Who had glory with whom, before the world was?"*
**Matt 3:16–17**: *"The Son in the water, the Spirit descending, the Father speaking. Who is who?"*
**John 1:1–2**: *"How can the Word be* with *God and* be *God?"*
**John 8:17–18**: *"Jesus counts Himself and the Father as two witnesses. Is one person two witnesses?"*
**John 14:16–17**: *"The Son asks the Father to send another Helper. How many are in that sentence?"*
**Eph 2:8–9**: *"Saved through faith, not of works. Where do the formula and tongues fit?"*

offense.title: Who was Jesus talking to?
offense.subtitle: Father and Son are distinct persons

altOpeners.text: *"At Jesus' baptism, whose voice came from heaven?"*

chain.text: **Matt 3:16–17**: The Son is baptized, the Spirit descends like a dove, the Father says, "This is My beloved Son." *"Is that one person in three places, or three persons?"*
**John 5:20; John 3:35**: The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. *"Can a person love and show things to his own human nature?"*

**John 8:16–18**: The Law requires two witnesses. Jesus says, "I am He who bears witness about Myself, and the Father who sent Me bears witness about Me." *"If they are one person, how many witnesses is that?"*
**John 12:28**: "Father, glorify Your name." A voice answers from heaven. *"Is that a conversation, or a monologue?"*
**John 17:1–5**: The Son speaks to the Father as "You" and to Himself as "Me," and speaks of glory they shared before the world was. *"Before there was any human nature, who was with whom?"*
**John 14:16–17, 26**: "I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Helper." *"Count them."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That was His human nature praying to His divine nature."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Natures don't pray; persons do. And John 17:5 speaks of glory shared **before the world was**, before there was any humanity to pray. *"Who is 'Me' and who is 'You' before Bethlehem?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"'I and the Father are one' (John 10:30)."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Amen, one in being. But the verb is plural: "I and the Father, **we are** one." He did not say "I am the Father." And the verse before distinguishes "My hand" and "My Father's hand."

ifTheySay.theySay: *"'He who has seen Me has seen the Father' (John 14:9)."*
ifTheySay.youSay: The next verse reads, "I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me… the Father abiding in Me does His works." He reveals the Father perfectly because He is God the Son. He does not say He is the Father. (John 1:18)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Isaiah 9:6 calls Him 'Everlasting Father.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: It is a title of the Messiah-King: literally "Father of eternity," the one who is eternal and cares for His people as a father. The same book has Yahweh sending His Servant and His Spirit (Isa 48:16). Nowhere does the New Testament call Jesus "the Father."

opener.text: *"When Jesus prayed in the garden, who was He praying to?"*

closer.text: *"The Father so loved the world that He gave His Son. That gift only means something if the Son is someone the Father could give. Do you know Him as He has shown Himself?"* (John 3:16; 1 John 2:23)

altOpeners.text: *"Who made all things: the Father alone, or the Father through the Son?"*

chain.text: **John 1:1–3, 14**: The Word was with God, was God, made all things, and became flesh. *"Is the Word a 'He' who was with God, or only a plan in God's mind?"*
**Col 1:13–17**: All things were created through the **Son** and for Him, and He is before all things. *"Which Son made the world?"*
**Heb 1:1–3, 8–10**: God made the world through His Son, and says **to the Son**, "Your throne, O God, is forever." *"Who is speaking to whom?"*
**John 6:38; John 3:13**: "I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me." *"Who came down, and who sent Him?"*
**Phil 2:5–7**: He existed in the form of God and then took the form of a slave. *"Who decided to humble Himself before becoming man?"*
**Gal 4:4**: "God sent forth His Son, born of a woman." *"Was He the Son when He was sent, or only after He arrived?"*

**John 11:41–42**: At Lazarus' tomb Jesus thanks the Father aloud "so that they may believe that You sent Me." Abner Chou's point on "sent" in John: what is sent already exists, no one sends himself, and the one sent represents the sender. So the Son existed before Bethlehem, is distinct from the Father, and bears His full authority. *"Can a person send himself?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"'The Son' is the humanity that began at Bethlehem (Luke 1:35)."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Luke 1:35 says why the child would be **called** Son of God. It does not say the Son began then. The Son made the world (Col 1:16; Heb 1:2). A human nature that did not yet exist made nothing.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Word was God's thought or plan, not a person."*
ifTheySay.youSay: A plan is not "with God" face to face, does not make all things, and is not called "He" and "the only begotten from the Father." (John 1:2–3, 14, 18)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"God is a Spirit, and Jesus is that Spirit in flesh."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God is spirit, yes. And the Spirit is sent by the Father and the Son and is called "another" Helper (John 14:16; John 15:26). Jesus is the Son incarnate, not the Father or the Spirit incarnate.

opener.text: *"Did the Son of God exist before Mary conceived?"*

closer.text: *"The One who died for sinners is the eternal Son, who was with the Father before the world was and came down out of love. Will you trust Him as He is?"* (John 17:24; Gal 2:20)

altOpeners.text: *"Is a person saved by what Christ did, or by Christ plus being baptized with the right words?"*

chain.text: **Eph 2:8–9**: By grace, through faith, not of works. *"Is baptism something done, or something believed?"*
**Rom 4:4–5**: God justifies the one who does not work but believes. *"When is he counted righteous?"*

**Acts 10:43–48**: Peter preaches forgiveness to everyone who believes. The Spirit falls while he is still speaking, **before** anyone is baptized. *"Were they God's people before the water or after?"*
**Acts 16:30–31**: "What must I do to be saved?" "Believe in the Lord Jesus." *"What did Paul leave out?"*
**1 Cor 1:14–17**: Paul thanks God he baptized few of them: "Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the gospel." *"Could he say that if baptism were part of the gospel?"*

**1 Cor 12:13, 29–30**: All believers were baptized by one Spirit into one body, and "All do not speak with tongues, do they?" *"If every believer has the Spirit and not all speak in tongues, can tongues be the proof?"*
**Matt 28:19**: Jesus' own command: "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit." *"Whose words should a church baptize with?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Acts 2:38: be baptized 'for the forgiveness of your sins.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: Peter's very next sermons promise forgiveness to those who repent and believe, with no mention of baptism (Acts 3:19; Acts 10:43). Baptism is the public confession of the repentance that receives forgiveness. Cornelius had the Spirit before the water.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The apostles always baptized in Jesus' name, never 'Father, Son and Spirit.'"*
ifTheySay.youSay: "In the name of" means by the authority of and with reference to Jesus, as against John's baptism or a Jewish washing. Luke words it four different ways (Acts 2:38; Acts 8:16; Acts 10:48; Acts 19:5), which is not how anyone records a fixed formula.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Matthew 28:19 says 'name,' singular, and that name is Jesus."*
ifTheySay.youSay: One name because one God. Then three are listed, each with "the": the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. That is the Trinity in one sentence.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"You haven't received the Holy Ghost unless you've spoken in tongues."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Anyone who does not have the Spirit does not belong to Christ at all, and every believer is sealed with the Spirit when he believes. (Rom 8:9; Eph 1:13–14) Our church also holds that the sign gifts ceased with the apostles.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"John 3:5: born of water and the Spirit."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Jesus expected Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel, to know this from the Old Testament: clean water and a new Spirit in Ezekiel 36:25–27. It is the new birth God gives, and the same chapter says whoever believes has eternal life. (John 3:10, 16)

opener.text: *"If a man repents and trusts Christ on his deathbed and never gets to the water, is he saved?"*

closer.text: *"Christ said, 'It is finished.' You can rest on that today, without one more step to make it count. Will you turn from sin and trust Him alone?"* (John 19:30; Rom 5:1)

defense.objection: "The Trinity is three gods."
defense.response: It is not, and say so first. One God, one Being. Within that one Being are three persons who are each fully God. Three gods would be three beings. Most people who reject the Trinity are rejecting something Christians do not believe.
defense.askBack: *"If I told you I believe in one God, not three, what would you say the Trinity is?"*

defense.objection: "The word 'Trinity' isn't in the Bible."
defense.response: Neither is "Oneness," "incarnation" or "Bible." The question is whether the teaching is there: one God; the Father, the Son and the Spirit are each God; and they are distinct from one another. Believe all three and you have the Trinity.
defense.askBack: *"Which of those three statements does Scripture not teach?"*

defense.objection: "The Trinity was invented at Nicaea in 325."
defense.response: Nicaea was about whether the Son is fully God, against Arius. Long before it, Christians baptized in the threefold name and were already rejecting the teaching that the Father and the Son are one person (it was called Sabellianism in the third century).
defense.askBack: *"If it began in 325, why does Matthew 28:19 read the way it does?"*

defense.objection: "'In Him all the fullness of Deity dwells in bodily form.' Jesus is all of God."
defense.response: Amen: Jesus is fully God, nothing lacking. That is the deity of the Son. It does not say the Son is the Father. The same letter thanks "the Father" who transferred us to the kingdom of "His beloved Son."
defense.askBack: *"Who is the Father of the beloved Son in chapter 1?"*

defense.objection: "God was manifest in the flesh (1 Tim 3:16)."
defense.response: We agree that God the Son became flesh. "The Word became flesh," and the Word was with God. It was the Son who was sent, not the Father.
defense.askBack: *"According to 1 John 4:14, who sent whom?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus said, 'I have come in My Father's name.' Jesus is the Father's name."
defense.response: To come in someone's name is to come with his authority. In the same breath Jesus says another may come "in his own name." He comes from the Father and is not the Father.
defense.askBack: *"Can you be sent by yourself?"*

defense.objection: "Zechariah 14:9: Yahweh will be one, and His name one."
defense.response: Yes, there is one Yahweh. The New Testament shows the Father, the Son and the Spirit sharing that one name and that one glory, which God gives to no other.
defense.askBack: *"If God gives His glory to no other, who shared it with the Father before the world was?"*

defense.objection: "Father, Son and Spirit are titles, like I'm a father, a son and a husband."
defense.response: That is one person with three roles, and it is the old error of modalism. A man who is a father and a son does not talk to himself, send himself or love himself as another. The Father, Son and Spirit do all three.
defense.askBack: *"Does your 'father' role ever speak to your 'son' role?"*

defense.objection: "If there are three persons, which one will we see in heaven?"
defense.response: We will see the Lamb, and John sees Him standing before the One who sits on the throne, and takes the scroll from His hand. Stephen saw Jesus standing at God's right hand.
defense.askBack: *"In Revelation 5, who hands the scroll to whom?"*

defense.objection: "Baptism in the titles is not valid. You need to be rebaptized in Jesus' name."
defense.response: Baptism "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" is what Jesus commanded. Nothing in Acts corrects it, and no one is ever said to be lost for the wording used over him. A sinner is saved through faith.
defense.askBack: *"Where does Scripture say someone was not saved because of the words said at his baptism?"*

defense.objection: "Holiness standards: no jewelry, uncut hair, long dresses. Without holiness no one will see the Lord."
defense.response: Holiness is commanded, and it is the fruit of a new heart, not the price of entry. Scripture warns about rules of "do not handle, do not taste, do not touch," which look wise and have no power against the flesh.
defense.askBack: *"Is holiness the root of salvation, or its fruit?"*

defense.objection: "We have the full gospel. Other churches only have part."
defense.response: The gospel Paul received and delivered is Christ's death for our sins, His burial and His resurrection, received by faith. Anything added as a requirement is another gospel.
defense.askBack: *"In 1 Corinthians 15, what does Paul call 'the gospel' by which you are saved?"*

items.text: "You just need the Holy Ghost, then you'd understand." (Answer: *"The Spirit wrote John 17. Would you read it with me?"*)
"I know what I felt." (Don't attack the experience. Ask what Scripture says God is like, and leave John 17:5.)
"My pastor can explain that." (Offer to meet with both of them, and give Rom 4:4–5 to read first.)
Repeating Acts 2:38. (Ask them to read Acts 10:43–48 aloud and say when those people received the Spirit.)

beliefs.text: There is no creed, on purpose: belief matters less than behavior. Jesus is a teacher and example whose way leads to wholeness, and other religions are valid paths too; their own statement says "the Spirit moves in beneficial ways in many faith traditions" [ProgressiveChristianity.org, Core Values]. The Bible is a human record of people's experience of God, inspiring but mistaken in places and to be corrected by modern knowledge and experience. Their own writers say many of them reject original sin, hell, the virgin birth, the bodily resurrection, and that Jesus died bearing God's wrath in the sinner's place. Sin is mostly injustice in society, salvation is healing here and now, and love means affirming people as they are.
