opener.text: *"Can a person be declared righteous by God today, completely, and know it?"*

closer.text: *"The tax collector didn't bring a process, just a plea, and went home justified. Will you stop leaning on your progress and trust Christ's finished work today (Luke 18:13–14; Rom 4:5)?"*

altOpeners.text: *"When Israel made the golden calf, who did Aaron say they were worshiping?"* (Ex 32:4–5: a "feast to Yahweh.")

chain.text: **Ex 20:4–5**: Not just making; "you shall not worship them or serve them." *"Is the act of bowing itself in view?"*
**Deut 4:15–19**: "You did not see any form on the day Yahweh spoke," so don't make one. *"Why does Moses ground it in what they *didn't* see?"*
**Ex 32:4–5**: The calf was meant to honor Yahweh, and God still judged it. *"Does good intention make a bowed-to image acceptable?"*

**2 Kings 18:4**: Hezekiah smashed the bronze serpent, an object *God commanded* (Num 21:8–9), because Israel burned incense to it. *"If a God-commanded image became an idol when venerated, what about one God never commanded?"*
**John 4:23–24**: The Father seeks those who worship "in spirit and truth." **Col 1:15**: Christ *is* the image of the invisible God. *"Do we need another image to reach the true Image?"*
**1 John 5:21**: "Guard yourselves from idols," written to Christians after the Incarnation.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"We give icons veneration, not worship (latria); the honor passes to the prototype [Nicaea II; CCC 2132 says the same]."*
ifTheySay.youSay: That is their position. The commandment forbids the bowing, not just a wrong inner attitude. Schooping, a former Orthodox priest, asks how mere "veneration" of an image becomes worship of Christ: if it doesn't, it's too little for Christ; if it does, it's worship given through an image.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"God commanded cherubim in the tabernacle (Ex 25:18)."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Yes, images can exist. But no one was ever told to bow to, kiss or pray before them, and the bronze serpent shows what happens when they do (2 Kings 18:4).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Incarnation made God visible, so we can picture Him."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God made Himself visible *in Christ* (John 14:9). Ortlund documents that early Christians did not bow to images, and that icon veneration came later; he notes that Epiphanius opposed it in the 4th century.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Nicaea II anathematizes people who refuse to venerate icons."*
ifTheySay.youSay: It does: "If anyone does not salute such representations… let him be anathema" [Nicaea II, anathemas]. Ask gently: *"Was every Christian before 787 who didn't kiss icons under a curse?"*

opener.text: *"Does the second commandment forbid only making images, or also bowing down to them?"* (Ex 20:5)

closer.text: *"Christ is the Image of God, and He invites you to come to Him directly, by faith, with no object in between (Heb 4:16; 10:19–22). Will you?"*

altOpeners.text: *"Was Jesus punished in our place, or only defeating death for us?"*

chain.text: **Isa 53:5–6**: "Pierced through for *our* transgressions… Yahweh has caused the iniquity of us all to fall on Him." *"Is that substitution?"*
**Isa 53:10**: "Yahweh was pleased to crush Him… a guilt offering." *"Who is acting in this verse?"*
**Gal 3:13**: Christ redeemed us from the curse "having become a curse for us." *"Whose curse did He bear?"*
**2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 2:24; 3:18**: Made sin for us; bore our sins in His body; "the just for the unjust." *"In whose place?"*
**Rom 3:25–26**: A propitiation, so that God is "just and the justifier." *"Why does God's justice need to be shown at the cross?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That makes the Father a vengeful pagan god punishing a 'whipping boy' [OCA EOCB, pp. 186–88]."*
ifTheySay.youSay: We reject that caricature too. Father and Son act together in love (John 10:17–18; Rom 8:32; 1 John 4:10). The OCA manual itself affirms that justification "stands alongside others" as a biblical metaphor [EOCB p. 188]. This isn't a conciliar dogma for them, so ask what *this* person believes.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"It's Anselm's medieval theory."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Isaiah 53 is seven centuries before Christ. Schooping, a former Orthodox priest, shows a substitutionary reading in Chrysostom and Theophylact.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The East teaches Christus Victor."*
ifTheySay.youSay: So does Scripture (Col 2:15; Heb 2:14–15). But Col 2:14 says the victory came by canceling "the certificate of debt" against us. Both are true together.

opener.text: *"In Isaiah 53, whose iniquity did Yahweh lay on the Servant?"*

closer.text: *"He bore the penalty in your place, and He offers you His righteousness as a gift (2 Cor 5:21). Will you turn from your sin and receive it by faith?"*

altOpeners.text: *"Do you believe we inherit only death from Adam, or also guilt?"* (The OCA says "only Adam and Eve are guilty of that sin" [OCA Q&A, "Original Sin"].)

chain.text: **Eph 2:1–3**: "Dead in your trespasses… by nature children of wrath." *"Does a neutral nature deserve wrath?"*

**Rom 5:12, 18–19**: "Through one transgression there resulted condemnation to all men… through the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners." *"Condemnation is a guilty verdict, not only a sickness, right?"*
**Ps 51:5**: "In sin my mother conceived me." *"When does David trace his sin back to?"*
**John 3:3–7**: "You must be born again." *"Can the dead cooperate in their own birth?"*
**Eph 2:4–9**: "But God… made us alive… by grace you have been saved… not of works." *"Who did the raising?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That's Augustine. The East never accepted original guilt."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Paul wrote Rom 5 centuries before Augustine. Also note that the Confession of Dositheus says infants "are subject to original sin" and need its remission [Decree 16], so Orthodox sources themselves aren't unanimous.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Then infants who die go to hell?"*
ifTheySay.youSay: Our hope rests in God's mercy and character (2 Sam 12:23). It doesn't rest on denying what Rom 5 says about Adam.

opener.text: *"Before God made us alive, how does Paul describe us: sick or dead?"* (Eph 2:1)

closer.text: *"Dead people don't need coaching. They need resurrection, and only Christ gives it, by grace through faith (Eph 2:4–9). Will you ask Him for that life?"*

defense.objection: "Sola Scriptura is a 16th-century invention."
defense.response: The fathers treated Scripture as the final court, including *Eastern* fathers. Athanasius: "the sacred and inspired Scriptures are sufficient to declare the truth." Cyril of Jerusalem: don't believe even me without proof from Scripture.
defense.askBack: *"Were Athanasius and Cyril Protestants?"*

defense.objection: "The Church is the pillar and ground of the truth (1 Tim 3:15)."
defense.response: Philaret uses this verse [Q18]. The context is a local congregation with elders and deacons. A pillar holds up the truth; it doesn't author it.
defense.askBack: *"Does a pillar make the truth or hold it up?"*

defense.objection: "Hold the traditions, by word or letter (2 Thess 2:15)."
defense.response: Philaret quotes this verse *to say tradition must agree with Scripture* [Q23]. Paul's tradition is the gospel (2:14), not a separate source.
defense.askBack: *"Your catechism says tradition must agree with Scripture. So which one tests the other?"*

defense.objection: "We are the one true Church; you split off."
defense.response: The Church is all who are united to Christ by faith (Eph 2:19–22). Our church holds that each local church is self-governing under Christ. Schooping, from the inside, calls Orthodox ecclesiology "inextricably exclusive".
defense.askBack: *"Is someone who trusts Christ alone, outside your communion, in Christ?"*

defense.objection: "We have apostolic succession from the apostles."
defense.response: Apostles had to be eyewitnesses of the risen Christ (Acts 1:21–22); the foundation was laid once (Eph 2:20). The succession Paul commands is of *teaching* (2 Tim 2:2). He warned that men in the succession would rise up teaching error (Acts 20:29–30).
defense.askBack: *"Can a bishop in succession teach error?"*

defense.objection: "Theosis: 'God became man so man might become god.'"
defense.response: Ask what they mean first. They do *not* mean sharing God's essence (they distinguish essence and energies). We agree on union with Christ and glorification (Rom 8:29–30; 1 John 3:2). We differ on making it a cooperative process that grounds acceptance with God.
defense.askBack: *"Is theosis the ground of your acceptance with God, or the fruit of it?"*

defense.objection: "Salvation is synergy: God and I working together."
defense.response: Philaret: a right faith "and good works" are necessary "to save one's own soul" [Q3]. Scripture says God gives the faith and raises the dead (Eph 2:5, 8–9; John 6:44). We work *out* what He has worked *in* (Phil 2:12–13).
defense.askBack: *"In Phil 2:13, who is doing the working?"*

defense.objection: "Icons have always been part of the Church."
defense.response: Ortlund documents that early Christians did not bow to or kiss images, and that 4th-century voices like Epiphanius opposed it. Veneration was defined in 787 [Nicaea II].
defense.askBack: *"Can you show icon veneration in the New Testament?"*

defense.objection: "Mary is the Theotokos."
defense.response: The title means "God-bearer," and it was first used to guard a truth we hold: the One she bore is truly God (Luke 1:35, 43). But she is mother to His humanity. His deity has no mother and no beginning (John 1:1; Mic 5:2). Scripture's own name for her is "the mother of Jesus" (Acts 1:14). We part ways where the title is used to lift her up, pray to her, or call her ever-virgin.
defense.askBack: *"Do you mean she bore the One who is God, or that she shares in His glory?"*

defense.objection: "Mary is ever-virgin."
defense.response: Philaret teaches it [Q186]. Matt 1:25 says "until she gave birth," and the Gospels name His brothers alongside His mother (Matt 13:55–56; Mark 6:3). Orthodox usually explain these as Joseph's children from an earlier marriage. The plain sense is siblings.
defense.askBack: *"What would Mark write if he meant siblings?"*

defense.objection: "Asking the saints to pray is like asking a friend."
defense.response: The OCA manual says this, and adds that the saints help and heal "themselves" too [EOCB p. 72]. Scripture models asking the living (James 5:16), never the departed, and gives us direct access through Christ (Heb 4:16; 7:25). Busenitz notes how such practices developed historically, citing Calvin's *Treatise on Relics*.
defense.askBack: *"Who does Hebrews tell you to approach for help in time of need?"*

defense.objection: "Baptism saves (John 3:5; 1 Pet 3:21)."
defense.response: Dositheus: without baptism "none is able to be saved" [Decree 16]. But the Spirit came on Cornelius before baptism (Acts 10:44–48), and Peter says baptism saves "not [as] the removal of dirt… but an appeal to God." Spurgeon: "Baptism without faith saves no one."
defense.askBack: *"Was the thief on the cross saved?"*

defense.objection: "The Eucharist is truly His body and blood."
defense.response: Dositheus affirms a change of substance [Decree 17]. Our church holds that the elements represent Christ's body and blood, *and* that the Supper is a real communion with the risen Christ (1 Cor 10:16). Jesus' words are spirit (John 6:63), and His sacrifice is not repeated (Heb 10:14, 18).
defense.askBack: *"Does the Supper proclaim His death, or offer it again?"*

defense.objection: "God isn't angry. Sin is sickness, not crime."
defense.response: Sin is both disease and guilt. Scripture speaks of wrath (Rom 1:18; John 3:36) and of a verdict (Rom 5:18). The OCA manual itself keeps "justification (our acquittal)" as a biblical theme [EOCB p. 188].
defense.askBack: *"Does John 3:36 say the wrath 'abides' or 'heals'?"*

defense.objection: "We don't inherit guilt, only death."
defense.response: The OCA says so [Q&A, "Original Sin"]. Rom 5:18–19 says one man's disobedience brought "condemnation to all men" and "made" many sinners. Dositheus speaks of infants' "original sin" [Decree 16].
defense.askBack: *"What does 'condemnation to all men' mean?"*

defense.objection: "Our church is 2,000 years old; yours is 500."
defense.response: The test is whether a church holds the apostles' teaching (Acts 2:42; Gal 1:8). Age doesn't settle it: the Pharisees' traditions were old too (Mark 7:13). Busenitz shows Scripture-alone convictions in the early church.
defense.askBack: *"If a 2,000-year-old church taught error, how would anyone know?"*

defense.objection: "The Divine Liturgy is ancient and beautiful. Protestant worship is shallow."
defense.response: Shallow worship anywhere is a fault, but age and beauty do not make worship true. Justin Martyr (c. 150) describes the early service as reading the apostles and prophets, preaching, prayer, and the Supper. Letham's concern is that Orthodoxy downplays preaching. Tozer: God tired of rituals that pointed ahead; Christ fulfilled them.
defense.askBack: *"What did the earliest services you can document center on?"*

defense.objection: "Toll houses / the soul's journey after death."
defense.response: Toll houses are not dogma, even in ROCOR, which declined to define them in 1980. Don't argue it as if it were their official teaching. Scripture: to be absent from the body is to be at home with the Lord (2 Cor 5:8; Luke 23:43).
defense.askBack: *"Is that a teaching you're bound to, or a pious opinion?"*

defense.objection: "God is known in His energies, not His essence. Theology is experience, not propositions."
defense.response: Keep it short. God truly reveals Himself in His word, and we can know Him truly, though not exhaustively (John 17:3; 1 Tim 6:16). Letham's concern is that Palamas's framework can lead to agnosticism about God. Then bring it back to the gospel.
defense.askBack: *"Can God tell us true things about Himself in words?"*

defense.objection: "We pray for the departed, and our prayers help them."
defense.response: The Confession of Dositheus says that some who repented without bearing fruit go to Hades and are delivered by "the prayers of the priests" and the good works of their relatives [Decree 18]. They will say it is not purgatory. It is still a second chance after death, and Scripture gives none. Scripture teaches that death is followed by judgment, that a great chasm is fixed, and that the believer who leaves the body is at home with the Lord. It never shows a prayer changing anyone's state after death.
defense.askBack: *"If today is the day of salvation, what are we telling people who plan to be prayed out later?"*

defense.objection: "Our infants are baptized, chrismated and given communion."
defense.response: That is their practice: baptized and chrismated infants receive communion [OCA, *The Orthodox Faith*, vol. 2]. It follows from believing that baptism gives new birth (see the baptism row). In Scripture those who "received his word" were baptized and then shared in the breaking of bread, and each person is told to examine himself before he eats. Our church baptizes believers, by immersion, and the Supper is for those who profess faith.
defense.askBack: *"Can an infant examine himself?"*

defense.objection: "I'd lose my family and my people if I left the Church."
defense.response: For many cradle Orthodox, church, family and nation are one thing, so this is the real obstacle. Don't wave it away. Jesus never hid the cost and promised that no one who leaves family for His sake will lose by it. Ask them to settle first who they are trusting.
defense.askBack: *"If it were true, would you want to know, even if it cost you?"*

items.text: "You have to experience the Liturgy to understand." (Accept the invitation kindly if you want to, then ask them to come read Romans 3–5 with you. Experience vs. Scripture is the whole question.)
"You're reading the Bible outside the Church." (Say: *"Then let's read it with Cyril and Athanasius,"* and quote their Scripture-first lines.)
"Our differences are just Eastern vs. Western mindsets." (Agree that categories differ, then ask: *"Does Rom 4:5 mean the same thing in Greek as in English?"*)

beliefs.text: "I don't know whether there is a God." Some mean it softly: "I haven't seen enough to decide, and I'm open." Some mean it hard: "No one can know." Most hold that the evidence is not clear either way, that the many religions cancel each other out, and that the honest thing is to withhold judgment. In practice most live as though there is no God while leaving the question open.

lead.label: Their position
lead.text: "I don't know whether there is a God." Some mean it softly: "I haven't seen enough to decide, and I'm open." Some mean it hard: "No one can know." Most hold that the evidence is not clear either way, that the many religions cancel each other out, and that the honest thing is to withhold judgment. In practice most live as though there is no God while leaving the question open.

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Whether God can be known. The agnostic says He has not made Himself clear. Scripture says He has: in what He made, in the conscience, in His word and finally in His Son, so that not knowing is not a neutral place to stand. A life lived with the question left open is a life lived without Him. (Rom 1:19–20; Heb 1:1–2; Matt 12:30; John 3:19–20)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"Are you saying you don't know, or that nobody can know? And what would it take for you to know?"* (John 7:17)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: What can be known about God is evident, because God made it evident. The heavens declare His glory day after day. He is not far from each one of us. He promises, "You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart." And John wrote his Gospel so that a reader may believe that Jesus is the Christ and have life in His name. (Rom 1:19–20; Ps 19:1–2; Acts 17:27; Jer 29:13; John 20:30–31)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"If God wanted me to believe, He would make it obvious."* → He has. He made a universe, gave you a conscience, and walked into history, died and rose with witnesses. People who saw Jesus' miracles in person still did not believe. Jesus said that if someone will not hear Scripture, he will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead. The obstacle is rarely the evidence. (John 12:37; Luke 16:31; John 5:40; Rom 1:20)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"You don't have to know everything to know enough. Do you know you have done wrong? Do you know you will die?"* Those two are not open questions. God has fixed a day of judgment and given proof by raising Jesus from the dead, and He receives everyone who comes: "the one who comes to Me I will never cast out." (Heb 9:27; Acts 17:30–31; John 6:37; Isa 55:6–7)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: Honesty about what you know matters. Blind belief is no virtue, and plenty of religious claims are false. Humility before big questions is right. A person should want reasons.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: Find out which kind you are talking to. The open kind is often the easiest person to talk with: thank them for their honesty and invite them to look at the best evidence, Jesus Himself, by reading a Gospel. The hard kind has made a claim, and you can gently ask how he knows it. Either way, don't let the conversation stay in the head. The agnostic is not undecided about how to live; he has already chosen. Aim at the conscience as you would with an atheist, and see the [Atheist](/atheist) plays for more. (Acts 17:11; Rom 2:14–15; 1 Pet 3:15)

cheatCard.text: **Rom 1:19–20**: *"What does Paul say every person already knows, and from what?"*
**Jer 29:13**: *"What does God promise the one who really seeks Him?"*
**John 7:17**: *"What does Jesus say comes before knowing?"*
**John 20:30–31**: *"Why was this Gospel written? Have you read it?"*
**Luke 16:31**: *"Would more evidence really settle it?"*
**2 Cor 6:2**: *"When does God say the right time is?"*

altOpeners.text: *"If God did exist and wanted to be known, how would He do it?"*

chain.text: If they say no one can know: that is itself a claim to know something about God, namely that He cannot or has not made Himself known. *"How do you know that?"*

**Ps 19:1–2; Rom 1:19–20**: Creation is God speaking without words. His eternal power and divine nature are clearly seen in what has been made. *"When you look at the night sky, what do you honestly think?"*
**Rom 2:14–15**: The conscience bears witness. You know some things are truly wrong. *"Where does that come from?"* See [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice).
**Heb 1:1–2**: God spoke long ago through the prophets, and in these last days has spoken in His Son. If there is a God who made speaking creatures, it is not strange that He speaks.

**John 1:18; John 14:9**: No one has seen God at any time; the only begotten God has explained Him. "He who has seen Me has seen the Father." *"If you wanted to know what God is like, would you look at Jesus?"*
**Acts 17:30–31**: God has given proof to all by raising Him from the dead. That is a claim about history, and it can be examined. See [The resurrection](/topic/the-resurrection).
**John 20:30–31**: These things are written so that you may believe. *"Would you read John's Gospel and tell me who you think Jesus is?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"There are thousands of religions. How could anyone pick?"*
ifTheySay.youSay: They are not all alike. Only one rests on a public event: a man who said He would rise and did. Start there, and the field narrows fast. See [The exclusivity of Christ](/topic/the-exclusivity-of-christ).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Science can't detect God."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Science studies what God made; it is the wrong tool for the Maker, as a metal detector is the wrong tool for finding wood. Science itself rests on things it cannot prove, like an orderly universe and a mind that can know it. See [Faith and reason](/topic/faith-and-reason).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"You can't be certain either."*
ifTheySay.youSay: My certainty does not rest on my mind but on God's word. Luke wrote so that we may know the certainty of these things, and John so that we may know we have eternal life. (Luke 1:3–4; 1 John 5:13; 2 Tim 1:12)

opener.text: *"When you say you don't know, do you mean you haven't looked into it, or that it can't be known?"*

closer.text: *"God is not hiding. He is 'not far from each one of us.' The question is not whether He can be known, but whether you want to know Him. Do you?"* (Acts 17:27; Jer 29:13)

altOpeners.text: *"How long have you been undecided? What are you doing to find out?"*

chain.text: The opener matters. If the answer is "no" or a long pause, the problem was never evidence. Say so kindly.

**John 3:19–20**: This is the judgment: the Light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the Light, for their deeds were evil. *"Is there anything you would have to give up if it were true?"*
**John 7:17**: "If anyone is willing to do His will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is of God." Willingness comes before knowing.
**Matt 12:30**: "He who is not with Me is against Me." There is no neutral seat. Not deciding is deciding.
**Prov 27:1; James 4:14**: Do not boast about tomorrow. You are a vapor that appears for a little while. *"What if the question closes before you answer it?"*
**Heb 9:27; Luke 12:20**: It is appointed for men to die once, and after this comes judgment. "This very night your soul is required of you."
**Isa 55:6–7; 2 Cor 6:2**: Seek Yahweh while He may be found. Now is the acceptable time. He will have compassion and abundantly pardon.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I'm keeping an open mind."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Good. An open mind, like an open mouth, is meant to close on something solid. Scripture describes people who are always learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. (2 Tim 3:7; Acts 17:11)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I'll look into it someday."*
ifTheySay.youSay: You plan for things far less certain than death. What would it cost to read one Gospel this month? (Luke 12:20; Ps 90:12)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"It doesn't really affect my life."*
ifTheySay.youSay: If there is a God, nothing affects it more: why you exist, what is right, and what happens when you die. "What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?" (Mark 8:36; Eccl 3:11)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I asked God to show Himself once and nothing happened."*
ifTheySay.youSay: He has not promised a sign on demand; He has given His word and His Son. Faith comes from hearing the word of Christ. Have you read it, asking Him to show you? (Rom 10:17; Luke 16:31; Jer 29:13)

opener.text: *"If I could show you that Christianity is true, would you become a Christian?"*

closer.text: *"You've been honest with me, so let me be honest with you: you already know enough to be accountable, and God has done enough for you to be forgiven. Will you come to Him?"* (Rom 1:20; John 6:37)

defense.objection: "There isn't enough evidence either way."
defense.response: Scripture says the evidence is everywhere and that the trouble is what we do with it. Ask what evidence would count, and who set that standard. See [Worldviews: how do you know?](/topic/worldviews-how-do-you-know).
defense.askBack: *"What would be enough?"*

defense.objection: "No one can know."
defense.response: That is a claim to know: that God, if He exists, could not make Himself known. Why not? The One who made the ear can speak.
defense.askBack: *"How do you know no one can know?"*

defense.objection: "All religions claim to be true. They can't all be right."
defense.response: Correct, they can't. That means some are false, not that none is true. Test the one that stakes everything on a resurrection in history.
defense.askBack: *"Have you examined the resurrection?"*

defense.objection: "I'm a good person. If there's a God, I'll be fine."
defense.response: That is not "I don't know"; that is confidence in your own record. By God's standard no one is good. See [The Way of the Master](/topic/the-way-of-the-master).
defense.askBack: *"Good by whose standard?"*

defense.objection: "It's arrogant to claim you know."
defense.response: It would be, if we had figured it out. We claim only that God has spoken and that we believe Him. Refusing what He says is not humility.
defense.askBack: *"Is it humble to tell God He hasn't been clear?"*

defense.objection: "I'd believe if God showed Himself to me."
defense.response: He showed Himself to a whole nation in Christ, and they crucified Him. He has given you their testimony. "Blessed are those who did not see, and yet believed."
defense.askBack: *"If He did, would you obey Him?"*

defense.objection: "I don't think about it much."
defense.response: God has set eternity in your heart; the question comes back at funerals and at 3 a.m. Wisdom thinks about its end before it arrives.
defense.askBack: *"What do you think happens when you die?"*

defense.objection: "I was raised religious and it didn't hold up."
defense.response: Ask what they were taught and what broke it. Often it was a church's failure or a thin version of the faith, not Christ. Offer to look at Jesus' own words together.
defense.askBack: *"Was it Jesus you rejected, or something else?"*

items.text: "I guess we'll find out when we die." (Say: *"That's the one time it's too late to change your answer. Would you look into it before then?"*)
"I need to think about it." (Good. Give them John's Gospel and one question: *"Who is Jesus?"*)
"Agree to disagree." (You haven't disagreed; they said they don't know. Offer to help them find out.)
"Nobody really knows." (Leave Jer 29:13.)

beliefs.text: There is a Creator, and reason and nature are enough to know it. But He does not step into the world: no miracles, no revelation, no incarnation, no answered prayer. The Bible is a human book, Jesus was a great moral teacher, and religion's doctrines were added by men. God wants people to be good, and good people can expect to be all right in the end. Few people use the word today, but a great many hold the belief: God exists, wants us to be nice and happy, stays out of the way unless needed, and takes good people to heaven. Sociologist Christian Smith named that "moralistic therapeutic deism" (2005).

lead.label: Their position
lead.text: There is a Creator, and reason and nature are enough to know it. But He does not step into the world: no miracles, no revelation, no incarnation, no answered prayer. The Bible is a human book, Jesus was a great moral teacher, and religion's doctrines were added by men. God wants people to be good, and good people can expect to be all right in the end. Few people use the word today, but a great many hold the belief: God exists, wants us to be nice and happy, stays out of the way unless needed, and takes good people to heaven. Sociologist Christian Smith named that "moralistic therapeutic deism" (2005).

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Whether God has spoken and acted. The deist's God made the world and went quiet. The God of Scripture upholds all things by the word of His power, feeds the sparrows, has spoken through prophets, and came in person. With that goes the gospel: the deist needs only to be decent; Scripture says he needs to be forgiven. (Heb 1:1–3; Col 1:17; John 1:14; Rom 3:23)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"If God cared enough to make you, why would He never say anything to you?"* (Heb 1:1–2)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: God did not leave Himself without witness: He gives rain and fruitful seasons. Not a sparrow falls apart from the Father, and the hairs of your head are numbered. He spoke through the prophets and, last of all, in His Son, who is the exact representation of His nature. The Word became flesh and dwelt among us. And He has fixed a day when He will judge the world. (Acts 14:17; Matt 10:29–30; Heb 1:1–3; John 1:14; Acts 17:30–31)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"Miracles break the laws of nature. A reasonable person can't accept them."* → You already believe the greatest miracle: that God made everything out of nothing. One who can do that can raise a dead man. The laws of nature describe how God ordinarily runs His world; they do not bind the Lawgiver. The question is not whether miracles can happen but whether one did. See [The resurrection](/topic/the-resurrection). (Gen 1:1; Jer 32:17; Acts 26:8)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"You believe God is just. Then what does a just God do with the wrong you have done?"* Nature can tell you there is a God, and conscience can tell you that you are guilty. Neither can tell you how to be forgiven. That takes news from God, and He sent it: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. (Rom 1:20; Rom 3:19; Rom 10:17; Rom 5:8)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: There is a Creator, and creation shows it. Reason is a gift and should be used. There is real right and wrong, and God cares about how we live. Superstition and priestly abuse of power are real evils.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: You are halfway there, so start with thanks: this person already grants God. Then press the two places deism is thin. First, it is odd for a God who makes persons to be silent toward them. Second, "be good" is no comfort to anyone honest about himself. Most deists have never examined the resurrection; they dismissed it in advance. Ask them to weigh it as history. With the churchgoing kind, who believes this while calling himself a Christian, use the commandments and the cross: see [The Gospel](/topic/the-gospel). (Acts 17:22–31; Rom 2:4; Acts 26:25–26)

cheatCard.text: **Heb 1:1–2**: *"Has God spoken? Through whom, last of all?"*
**Matt 10:29–30**: *"How involved is God, according to Jesus?"*
**Acts 14:17**: *"What witness has God left of Himself every day?"*
**Acts 26:8**: *"If God made the world, why is raising the dead incredible?"*
**Luke 18:19**: *"Who does Jesus say is good?"*
**Rom 5:8**: *"What did God do that nature could never tell you?"*

altOpeners.text: *"Would a father build a house for his children and never speak to them?"*

chain.text: **Ps 19:1–4**: Start where they are. The heavens declare the glory of God. *"What does creation tell you about Him?"* Power, intelligence, order. Agree.

**Ps 94:9**: "He who planted the ear, does He not hear? He who formed the eye, does He not see?" The Maker of persons who speak and love is not less than personal. *"Can the One who invented language be unable to use it?"*

**Acts 17:24–28**: He made the world, gives to all life and breath, set the times and boundaries of nations so that they would seek Him, and is not far from each of us. In Him we live and move and exist.
**Col 1:16–17; Heb 1:3**: All things were created through Christ, and in Him all things hold together. The world is not a wound-up clock; it is upheld every moment.
**Matt 6:26; Matt 10:29–31**: Your Father feeds the birds. Not one sparrow falls without Him. *"That is Jesus' picture of God. Was He wrong about His Father?"*
**Heb 1:1–2; 2 Pet 1:20–21**: God spoke through the prophets, and men moved by the Holy Spirit spoke from God. See [Is the Bible reliable?](/topic/is-the-bible-reliable).
**John 1:14, 18**: The Word became flesh. God did not send a message only; He came.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Why would the God of a hundred billion galaxies care about us?"*
ifTheySay.youSay: Size is not worth. A father values his child over his house. Scripture asks the same question in wonder and answers that God is mindful of man. (Ps 8:3–5; Matt 10:31)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Revelation to one small nation long ago is unfair to everyone else."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God chose one nation so that through it all the families of the earth would be blessed, and the message has gone to every tongue. No one is judged for light he did not have; everyone has enough to be accountable. (Gen 12:3; Rev 7:9; Rom 1:20; Rom 2:12)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Prayer changes nothing. Things just take their course."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Jesus taught the opposite and prayed Himself. A Father who knows how to give good gifts hears His children. (Matt 7:11; James 5:16; 1 John 5:14)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Evil and suffering show God is not involved."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Or they show a world in rebellion that He has not yet judged, out of patience. At the cross He used the worst evil for the greatest good. See [The problem of evil](/topic/the-problem-of-evil). (Gen 50:20; Acts 2:23; 2 Pet 3:9)

opener.text: *"You believe God made everything. What do you think He is doing now?"*

closer.text: *"You believe in a God who made you. He is nearer than you thought, He has spoken, and He has come. Would you listen to what He said?"* (Acts 17:27; Heb 1:2)

offense.title: Good enough for God?
offense.subtitle: the moral teacher and the Savior

altOpeners.text: *"You admire Jesus as a teacher. What do you make of what He said about Himself?"*

chain.text: **Matt 22:37–39**: Jesus summed up what God wants: love God with all your heart, soul and mind, and your neighbor as yourself. *"Have you done that, even for one day?"*
**Matt 5:21–22, 27–28**: The moral teacher raised the bar: anger is murder in the heart, and lust is adultery in the heart. His ethics do not flatter us; they convict us.
**Luke 18:19; Rom 3:10–12**: "No one is good except God alone." None is righteous, not even one.
**Rom 2:5–6**: A just God will repay each person according to his works. *"You believe God is just. Is that good news for you?"*

**Mark 2:5–7; John 8:58**: Jesus did not only teach. He forgave sins as only God can, and said, "Before Abraham was born, I am." A mere moral teacher who says that is not moral. *"Was He lying, deluded, or telling the truth?"*
**Mark 10:45**: He said He came to give His life as a ransom for many. His own account of His mission is the cross, not the Sermon on the Mount.
**1 Cor 15:3–6; Acts 17:31**: He died for our sins, was buried, was raised and was seen by more than five hundred. God gave proof to all by raising Him.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I keep the Golden Rule. That's enough."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Do you keep it? Always? And it is the second commandment; the first is to love God with everything. (Matt 7:12; Matt 22:37–38; James 2:10)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The miracles and the claims to be God were added later by the church."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Paul's letters, written within about twenty-five years of the cross, already worship Jesus as Lord and report the resurrection from eyewitnesses then living. There was no time for legend. (1 Cor 15:3–8; Phil 2:6–11)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Jefferson cut out the miracles and kept the morals."*
ifTheySay.youSay: He did, with a razor. What he kept is a teacher who claims authority over every conscience and then dies for nothing. The Jesus of history comes whole or not at all. (John 10:37–38; Luke 24:25–27)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"A good God would not condemn decent people."*
ifTheySay.youSay: A good judge does not ignore crimes because the criminal was polite. And He has done more than be fair: He bore the sentence Himself. See [Hell and eternal judgment](/topic/hell-and-eternal-judgment). (Prov 17:15; Rom 3:25–26)

opener.text: *"What do you think God wants from people?"*

closer.text: *"Deism gives you a Maker and a standard, and leaves you alone with your record. The gospel gives you a Father and a Savior. Which do you need?"* (Rom 5:8; John 1:12)

defense.objection: "God set things in motion and stepped back."
defense.response: Scripture says He upholds all things by the word of His power, right now. Jesus said His Father is working until now.
defense.askBack: *"How do you know He stepped back?"*

defense.objection: "Reason is enough. I don't need revelation."
defense.response: Reason can find that there is a God. It cannot find out what He thinks of you or how to be forgiven. For that He has to tell you.
defense.askBack: *"Can reason tell you whether God will forgive you?"*

defense.objection: "Miracles don't happen."
defense.response: If God made the universe, miracles are possible. Whether one happened is a question of testimony. Look at the resurrection.
defense.askBack: *"Is that a conclusion from evidence, or an assumption before it?"*

defense.objection: "The Bible is just men's writings."
defense.response: It claims more, Jesus treated it as God's word, and its fulfilled prophecy backs the claim. See [Is the Bible reliable?](/topic/is-the-bible-reliable).
defense.askBack: *"Have you read it as an adult?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was a great moral teacher, nothing more."
defense.response: He claimed to forgive sins, to judge the world and to exist before Abraham. A man who says that falsely is not a great moral teacher.
defense.askBack: *"Which of His claims would a mere teacher make?"*

defense.objection: "Organized religion is man-made and corrupt."
defense.response: Much of it is, and Jesus said so before you did. But the abuse of a thing does not make the thing false. He founded His church and gave Himself for her.
defense.askBack: *"Does counterfeit money mean there is no real money?"*

defense.objection: "Good people go to heaven."
defense.response: That is the most widely held belief in America and it is not in the Bible. No one is good; heaven is for the forgiven.
defense.askBack: *"How good is good enough, and who told you?"*

defense.objection: "God just wants me to be happy."
defense.response: He wants you holy, and in Him, truly happy. A God who exists to serve our plans is one we made in our own image.
defense.askBack: *"What if what you want and what is good for you differ?"*

defense.objection: "The Founding Fathers were deists."
defense.response: Some were, and many were not. Either way, truth is not settled by who held it.
defense.askBack: *"Is it true? That's the only question."*

items.text: "I believe in God, and that's enough." (Say: *"The demons also believe, and shudder. What matters is whether you are right with Him."* James 2:19.)
"I don't need church to be a good person." (Agree that church doesn't make anyone good, and ask: *"Are you good?"*)
"We can't know those details." (Ask: *"Unless He told us. Would you read what He said?"*)
"To each his own." (Leave Rom 5:8.)

beliefs.text: There is no God and no life after death, and human beings are the product of unguided evolution. Knowledge comes through science and reason. Right and wrong are worked out from human need and experience, not handed down. People are basically good and can be improved by education, science and fair institutions. Meaning is something we make. Their own summary: "No deity will save us; we must save ourselves" [Humanist Manifesto II, 1973]. Many would simply say, "I believe in science and being a good person."

lead.label: Their position
lead.text: There is no God and no life after death, and human beings are the product of unguided evolution. Knowledge comes through science and reason. Right and wrong are worked out from human need and experience, not handed down. People are basically good and can be improved by education, science and fair institutions. Meaning is something we make. Their own summary: "No deity will save us; we must save ourselves" [Humanist Manifesto II, 1973]. Many would simply say, "I believe in science and being a good person."

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Who is the measure, God or man, and whether man can save himself. Humanism keeps the Bible's high view of human worth and throws away its foundation, the image of God. It also throws away the Bible's diagnosis, that the human heart is the problem, and so trusts the patient to cure himself. (Gen 1:27; Jer 17:5; Jer 17:9; Rom 1:25)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"You believe every human being has dignity and equal worth. If we are accidents of chemistry, where does that worth come from?"* (Gen 1:27)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: God created man in His own image. That is why human life is sacred, why it is wrong to curse or kill a man, and why all nations are of one blood. Yet the heart is deceitful above all else, and none is righteous. Do not trust in princes or in mortal man, in whom there is no salvation: his spirit departs, and his plans perish. (Gen 1:26–27; Gen 9:6; Acts 17:26; Jer 17:9; Rom 3:10–12; Ps 146:3–4)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"I can be good without God."* → You can do many good things, and I don't doubt you do. Scripture says why: you are made in God's image, and His law is written on your heart. But the question is not whether you can behave without believing. It is what makes anything good at all, and whether you are good by God's measure. Jesus said no one is. See [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice). (Rom 2:14–15; Luke 18:19; Rom 3:23)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"The manifesto says we must save ourselves. After a century of more education, science and wealth than any people in history, how is that going? How is it going in your own heart?"* We know the good and do not do it. The kindness of God appeared, and He saved us, not by deeds we had done, but by His mercy. (Rom 7:18–19; Rom 7:24–25; Titus 3:4–5; John 8:36)

lead.label: Where we agree
lead.text: Human beings matter. Cruelty, oppression and ignorance are evils worth fighting. Science is a good tool and truth should be followed. This life is precious. Hypocrisy in religion deserves criticism.

lead.label: Approach
lead.text: The humanist is living on borrowed capital: human rights, equality and compassion grew in soil the Bible plowed, and they do not grow from "matter in motion." Jeff Durbin's line to a skeptic says it well: "you're acting like a Christian." Affirm the good they love, then ask what it rests on. Do not argue that atheists are immoral; argue that their morality has no foundation and their optimism about man has no evidence. Then go to the conscience and the cross. The [Atheist](/atheist) plays and [Worldviews: how do you know?](/topic/worldviews-how-do-you-know) carry the rest. Remember that humanism is itself a faith with a creed, and its first manifesto called it religious. (Acts 17:22–31; Col 2:8; 1 Pet 3:15)

cheatCard.text: **Gen 1:27**: *"What gives a human being worth that an animal does not have?"*
**Jer 17:9**: *"Is the human heart the solution or the problem?"*
**Ps 146:3–4**: *"What happens to every human plan?"*
**Rom 7:18–19**: *"Do you always do the good you know?"*
**Mark 8:36**: *"What is the profit if you gain the world and lose your soul?"*
**Titus 3:4–5**: *"Who does the saving here?"*

offense.title: Where does human worth come from?
offense.subtitle: the image of God

altOpeners.text: *"Why is it wrong to treat people as things?"*

chain.text: Let them answer: reason, feeling, consciousness, contribution. Each of those comes in degrees, so worth would come in degrees: the infant, the disabled and the dying would have less. *"Do you believe that?"* They do not, and that is to their credit.
If we are the unplanned result of matter, time and chance, then "equal dignity" is a feeling one species has about itself. Nature knows nothing of equality; it knows strong and weak.
**Gen 1:26–27**: God created man in His own image, male and female. Worth is given, not earned, and it does not come in degrees.
**Gen 9:6; James 3:9**: That image is the reason murder is a crime against God and why it is wrong even to curse a man.
**Acts 17:26**: He made from one man every nation. Human equality and the unity of the race are Bible doctrines before they were modern ideals.
**Ps 8:3–5**: Small against the heavens, yet crowned with glory and majesty. Scripture explains both our smallness and our greatness.
**Mark 8:36–37; John 3:16**: Jesus put the value of one soul above the whole world, and God gave His Son for it. *"Nothing has ever set human worth higher than the cross."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"We give each other worth by agreement."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Then a society can agree to take it away, and has. Hitler's Germany agreed that Jews had none. If agreement is the standard, that was good for them at the time, and no outsider could call it evil. A right that the majority grants, the majority can revoke. Only a worth given by God stands over every government. (Acts 5:29; Prov 22:2)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Morality evolved because cooperation helps us survive."*
ifTheySay.youSay: That would explain why we feel obligations, not why we have any. And evolution "favors" cruelty as readily as kindness when it works. See [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Religion has done more harm than good."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Much evil has been done in God's name, against Christ's commands. But the worst slaughters of the last century were carried out by regimes that had officially abolished God. And look at who built the hospitals and ended the slave trade. Judge Christ by Christ. (Matt 7:16–20; James 1:27; John 13:35)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Science tells us what is true."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Science tells us what is, never what ought to be, and "only science gives knowledge" is not itself a finding of science. See [Faith and reason](/topic/faith-and-reason).

opener.text: *"What makes a human life valuable?"*

closer.text: *"You are right about human dignity and wrong about where it comes from. The God whose image you bear is the reason you care. Would you want to know Him?"* (Gen 1:27; Acts 17:27–28)

altOpeners.text: *"What would it take to fix the world?"*

chain.text: Ask why, if people are basically good, every society needs locks, police, passwords and contracts, and why no one has to teach a child to be selfish.
**Gen 6:5; Gen 8:21**: Every intent of the thoughts of man's heart was only evil continually; the intent of man's heart is evil from his youth. That was true before the flood and after it.
**Jer 17:9; Mark 7:21–23**: The heart is deceitful and desperately sick. Evil comes from within. Better schools make cleverer sinners; the most educated nation in Europe built the death camps.
**Rom 7:18–19**: "The good that I want, I do not do." *"Is that your experience? Do you live up to your own ideals?"*

**Ps 146:3–4; Eccl 2:16**: Whatever progress we make, each of us dies and his plans perish, and the wise man dies like the fool. Humanism has no answer to the grave. *"If death wins, in what sense have we saved ourselves?"*
**Ezek 36:26; John 3:3**: What we need is not improvement but a new heart, and that is what God promises: "I will give you a new heart." "You must be born again."

**1 Cor 15:21–22; Rom 5:19**: By a man came death, and by a Man came the resurrection of the dead. Christ is the true human being, the one who obeyed, and He gives His record and His life to those who trust Him.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Evil comes from poverty, ignorance and bad systems."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Those make things worse, and Christians should fight them. But the comfortable and educated sin as freely as anyone, only with better lawyers. Systems are made of hearts. (James 4:1–2; Mark 7:21)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"We make our own meaning."*
ifTheySay.youSay: A meaning you invent is a story you tell yourself, and it ends when you do. Solomon tried pleasure, work, wisdom and wealth and called it vapor. Meaning has to be given by the One who made you. (Eccl 1:2–3; Eccl 12:13–14; John 17:3)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"This life is all there is, so make the most of it."*
ifTheySay.youSay: Paul agrees that would follow: "If the dead are not raised, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." But Christ has been raised. See [The resurrection](/topic/the-resurrection). (1 Cor 15:32; 1 Cor 15:20)

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I don't need saving."*
ifTheySay.youSay: From what you have done, and from what is coming. Walk through a few commandments: see [The Way of the Master](/topic/the-way-of-the-master). (Rom 3:19; Heb 9:27)

opener.text: *"Do you think people are basically good?"*

closer.text: *"'No deity will save us; we must save ourselves.' That is not good news; that is a burden no one has carried. Here is good news: 'When the kindness of God our Savior appeared, He saved us.' Would you lay the burden down?"* (Titus 3:4–5; Matt 11:28)

defense.objection: "I believe in science, not faith."
defense.response: Science is a gift, and it was born among people who believed a rational God made an orderly world. It cannot tell you why you matter, what is right or what happens when you die.
defense.askBack: *"Which experiment shows that people have rights?"*

defense.objection: "Faith is believing without evidence."
defense.response: Not in the Bible. Jesus presented Himself alive by many convincing proofs, and the apostles appealed to public facts. Faith is trust in One who has shown Himself trustworthy.
defense.askBack: *"Where did you get that definition?"*

defense.objection: "Society decides what is right."
defense.response: Then what Hitler's Germany did to the Jews was right, there and then, and the people who hid Jews were the wrongdoers. And if you retreat to "each person decides," the rapist is never wrong. Neither holds, so the standard is above both. See [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice).
defense.askBack: *"Was the Holocaust wrong even though their society approved it?"*

defense.objection: "Morality is about human wellbeing."
defense.response: Whose wellbeing, measured how, and why should the strong care about the weak? "Wellbeing" quietly assumes that people have worth, which is the very thing to be explained.
defense.askBack: *"Why ought I to care about a stranger's wellbeing?"*

defense.objection: "People are basically good."
defense.response: History, the news and our own hearts say otherwise, and so does Jesus. The honest diagnosis is the first step to the cure.
defense.askBack: *"Do you need a lock on your door?"*

defense.objection: "Religion is the cause of most wars and oppression."
defense.response: Sinners are. They use religion, nation, race and economics alike. The officially godless states of the last century killed their own people by the tens of millions.
defense.askBack: *"What did the regimes that abolished God put in His place?"*

defense.objection: "Keep your religion out of public life."
defense.response: Everyone brings a view of what is good into public life. Humanism is one such view, with manifestos. The question is not whether a creed will shape the law, but which one.
defense.askBack: *"Is your view of right and wrong allowed in?"*

defense.objection: "When you're dead, you're dead."
defense.response: That is a belief, not a discovery. Scripture says judgment follows death, and God has given evidence by raising Jesus.
defense.askBack: *"How do you know?"*

defense.objection: "I find meaning in family, work and making things better."
defense.response: Those are good gifts. But gifts point to a Giver, and none of them survives the grave. You were made for more than what you can lose.
defense.askBack: *"What happens to that meaning when those are taken?"*

defense.objection: "Christianity is anti-human: guilt, rules and fear."
defense.response: It says you are made in God's image, loved at the cost of God's own Son, and offered life that death cannot end. Nothing has ever thought more of human beings. Guilt is real, and it is taken away.
defense.askBack: *"What would you do with guilt if there were no forgiveness?"*

items.text: "I'm glad it works for you." (Say: *"It only matters if it's true. Would you look at the evidence for the resurrection?"*)
"I just try to be a good person." (Ask: *"By whose standard, and how are you doing?"*)
"We'll never agree on this." (Leave the question from the card: *"Where does human worth come from?"*)
"Religion isn't for me." (Offer Jesus, not religion: *"Would you read one Gospel?"*)

beliefs.text: Atheist: usually "I don't believe in God" (some say "there is no God"). Agnostic: "I don't know" or "we can't know." Most hold that the universe and life came from natural causes alone and the Bible is a human book. Many see right and wrong as human-made.

lead.label: Their position
lead.text: Atheist: usually "I don't believe in God" (some say "there is no God"). Agnostic: "I don't know" or "we can't know." Most hold that the universe and life came from natural causes alone and the Bible is a human book. Many see right and wrong as human-made.

lead.label: The dividing issue
lead.text: Whether God has made Himself known. They say there is not enough evidence. Scripture says every person already knows God from creation and conscience and holds that truth down, because to admit Him is to admit we answer to Him. The problem is not the evidence; it is the heart. (Rom 1:18–21; Rom 2:14–15; Ps 14:1; John 3:19–20)

lead.label: Ask this question
lead.text: *"Is anything truly right or wrong, for everyone, everywhere? In a universe of only matter and chance, where does that come from?"* (Rom 2:14–15)

lead.label: Scriptural response
lead.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. The heavens declare His glory, and His eternal power and divine nature are clearly seen in what has been made, so that men are without excuse. The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge, and in Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. God now commands all people everywhere to repent, and has given proof by raising Jesus from the dead. (Gen 1:1; Ps 19:1; Rom 1:19–20; Prov 1:7; Col 2:3; Acts 17:30–31)

lead.label: Common objection
lead.text: *"There's no evidence for God."* → Everything is evidence: that there is a universe at all, that it is ordered, that you have a conscience, and that the laws of logic you are using right now are not made of atoms. The real question is who gets to set the standard of proof. Jesus said that those who will not hear Scripture will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead. See [Worldviews: how do you know?](/topic/worldviews-how-do-you-know) and [Faith and reason](/topic/faith-and-reason). (Luke 16:31; Rom 1:20)

lead.label: Gospel bridge
lead.text: *"You have a conscience. Have you kept even your own standard?"* Walk through a few commandments: see [The Way of the Master](/topic/the-way-of-the-master). It is appointed for men to die once, and after this comes judgment. The same God showed His love in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. (Rom 2:15–16; Heb 9:27; Rom 5:8; Acts 17:30–31)

lead.label: Mindset
lead.text: Scripture says every person knows God and suppresses that knowledge (Rom 1:18–21). The problem isn't missing evidence; it's the heart. The first move is to **make them define their position**, and they usually back off from "God doesn't exist" to "I don't know." Then aim at the conscience.

cheatCard.text: *"Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?"* (Sets the burden.)
*"Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"*
*"Life only comes from life. Where did the first life come from?"*
*"No one dies for what they **know** is a lie."* (1 Cor 15:3–8)
*"If heaven and hell were real, wouldn't you want to know before you die?"*
**Rom 1:18–21**: they know God and suppress it. Appeal to the conscience, not just the intellect.

chain.text: *"When you say you're an atheist, are you saying God doesn't exist, or that you lack belief?"* → If it's a claim: *"How do you know?"* If it's lack of belief: *"So you don't know. Would you want to know if God has spoken?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I just believe in one less god than you."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"You already reject gods who aren't there. I'm asking about the One you already know is there."* (Rom 1:19–21)

opener.text: *"Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?"*

chain.text: *"Have you ever experienced something as ordered and designed as this coming from something that isn't intelligent?"*
*"Life always comes from life. That's a scientific principle (biogenesis)."* Evolution talks about life that already exists **changing**. It doesn't explain where life **came from**.

*"Our planet is set for life: its distance from the sun, its tilt, its moon, its magnetic field. When you find that many settings exactly right, do you assume a setter?"* Give this as God's world speaking, not as a neutral coin toss. He formed the earth to be lived in. (Isa 45:18; Ps 19:1–4)
**Ps 19:1; Rom 1:20; Acts 17:24–28** ("in Him we live and move and have our being").

opener.text: *"Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"*

altOpeners.text: *"Where do you get this idea of bad from?"* (When they call something evil or unfair.)
*"What would count as evidence for you?"* (When they say there's no evidence for God.)
*"Is morality objective, or is it opinion?"* (When they say you're wrong about a moral issue.)

chain.label: Logic
chain.text: *"Are the laws of logic physical? Do they change? Where do universal, unchanging laws come from in a universe that's just matter in motion?"*

chain.label: Morality
chain.text: *"Is it **objectively** wrong to torture a child for fun? Wrong according to whom?"* → if they say it's subjective, then it's just preference. If they say it's objective, they need a transcendent standard. **Rom 2:14–15**, the law is written on the heart.

chain.label: Reason
chain.text: *"If your brain is just chemistry shaped for survival, not truth, why trust it to reason that God doesn't exist?"*

chain.label: Goal
chain.text: show they **use** God's world (logic, morality, reason) while denying Him (Rom 1:18–21; Prov 1:7). For the full approach, open [Worldviews: how do you know?](/topic/worldviews-how-do-you-know).

opener.text: *"Can I ask you about three things we both rely on every day: logic, right and wrong, and your own reasoning?"*

altOpeners.text: *"What about the people who didn't believe in Jesus, persecuted His followers, then said, 'I saw Jesus'?"* (When they say it's a game of telephone.)

chain.text: *"If Christ didn't rise from the dead, Christianity is false. Period."* (1 Cor 15:14–19) Christianity puts itself on a testable, historical claim, and God has given proof to all by raising Him from the dead (Acts 17:31).

chain.label: Facts
chain.text: crucified publicly under Pilate · the tomb was guarded · the disciples fled as cowards, then died boldly · hostile skeptics were converted (Paul the persecutor, James the doubting brother). *"Why would eyewitnesses and enemies suffer and die for what they **knew** was a lie?"*

opener.text: *"If Jesus really rose from the dead, would you become a Christian?"*

closer.text: *"If heaven and hell were real, wouldn't you want to know now? You wouldn't want to wait until you die to find out."*

defense.objection: "Jesus is a copy of Horus / Osiris / Mithras."
defense.response: Comes from pop media (*Zeitgeist*, *Religulous*), not the Egyptian sources. No virgin birth, no crucifixion, no resurrection in the primary texts.
defense.askBack: *"Which primary Egyptian text says Horus was born of a virgin? Name it."*

defense.objection: "It's like the Salem witch trials / a game of telephone."
defense.response: Public execution under Pilate, guarded tomb, and **eyewitnesses** who were still alive when it was written (1 Cor 15:6, "most are still alive").
defense.askBack: *"Who dies for what they know is a lie?"*

defense.objection: "Why do babies get cancer because Adam ate fruit?"
defense.response: Federal headship. A head affects those he represents, like a mother's toxins affecting her unborn child. Adam's fall broke creation. Christ, the second Adam, restores it.
defense.askBack: *"If God exists, wouldn't you expect Him to fix the fall? He did, in Christ."*

defense.objection: "If God knew I'd reject Him, why create me? That's unjust."
defense.response: God is just and owes no one mercy. No one is forced to reject Him: people reject Him because they love their sin, and they are responsible for it. Hell is the just penalty for real guilt, not a mistake. Yet God *freely* offers Christ to all who come, and no one who comes is turned away.
defense.goTo: Rom 9:19–21; John 3:19; Ezek 33:11; John 6:37; Rom 1:24 ("God **gave them up**")
defense.askBack: *"Is there anything you've done that a perfectly just judge should ignore?"*

defense.objection: "A jealous God who demands worship is vain."
defense.response: Not all jealousy is sinful. A husband who's jealous over an unfaithful wife is **rightly** jealous. God made every breath you take, so He has a rightful claim.
defense.askBack: *"If your wife slept with another man, would your jealousy be ugly, or just?"*

defense.objection: "Heaven/hell is a game show: pick a door."
defense.response: It's not a game show. It's a **command and an invitation**. God commands everyone to repent and offers Himself, the greatest good. Whoever refuses Him is responsible for that refusal. Full answer: [Hell and eternal judgment](/topic/hell-and-eternal-judgment).
defense.askBack: *"It's not God playing games. You're playing games with Him."*

defense.objection: "So many religions. How would I know which one?"
defense.response: God has spoken, and He proved it publicly by raising Jesus from the dead. Only Christianity rests on a public resurrection, an event that is **historically testable**. Full answer: [The exclusivity of Christ](/topic/the-exclusivity-of-christ).
defense.askBack: *"Which other religion stakes everything on a public event you can investigate?"*

defense.objection: "Who created God?"
defense.response: The question assumes everything needs a cause. It doesn't. Only what **begins to exist** needs a cause. God never began; He is uncaused by definition, the cause of everything outside Himself. Asking who made Him is a category mistake, like asking who made the One who was never made.
defense.askBack: *"Does everything need a cause, or only things that begin to exist?"*

defense.objection: "I'm not 100% sure. I have doubts."
defense.response: Faith isn't intellectual perfection. Jesus welcomes doubters who come to Him.
defense.askBack: *"Do you believe Christ died for your sins and rose again? Will you turn from your sin and trust Him as Lord?"*

defense.objection: "There's no evidence for God."
defense.response: Creation itself is the evidence: a universe that began, runs on laws, and holds minds and morals. And God gave proof to all by raising Jesus from the dead.
defense.askBack: *"What would count as evidence for you?"* Then: *"Is the problem the evidence, or that you don't want God to be there?"*

defense.objection: "Science has disproved God."
defense.response: Science studies how creation works. It depends on order and laws it cannot explain, and it cannot tell you why anything exists or what is right.
defense.askBack: *"Which experiment showed there is no God?"*

defense.objection: "If God is good, why is there so much evil and suffering?"
defense.response: Calling something evil assumes a real standard of good. Scripture names the cause (the fall), shows God turning evil to good, entering suffering at the cross, and promising to end it. Full answer: [The problem of evil](/topic/the-problem-of-evil).
defense.askBack: *"By what standard do you call it evil?"*

defense.objection: "The Bible was written by men and is full of errors."
defense.response: Men wrote as they were moved by the Holy Spirit. Ask for a specific error and read it together.
defense.askBack: *"Which error? Let's look at it."*

defense.objection: "Morality is decided by each person, or by society."
defense.response: If each person decides, the rapist is never wrong; he was acting on his own truth. If society decides, what Hitler's Germany did to the Jews was good for them at the time. No one can live with either. Real right and wrong need a standard above every person and nation. See [Morality and justice](/topic/morality-and-justice).
defense.askBack: *"Was the Holocaust wrong even though their society approved?"*

defense.objection: "The God of the Old Testament is a moral monster."
defense.response: To judge Him you need an objective standard, which only He supplies. He judged wicked nations after centuries of patience, He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, and He bore judgment Himself at the cross.
defense.askBack: *"If there is no God, what makes anything objectively wrong?"*

defense.objection: "Religion causes wars, and Christians are hypocrites."
defense.response: People sin, which is exactly what the Bible says. Jesus condemned hypocrisy harder than anyone. Judge Christianity by Christ.
defense.askBack: *"Does a counterfeit bill prove there's no real money?"*

defense.objection: "I'm a good person. I don't need God."
defense.response: Good by whose standard? By God's law, none is righteous, and breaking one point makes us guilty of all. Then give the gospel: Christ died for sinners.
defense.askBack: *"Have you ever lied, stolen, or hated someone? What does that make you before a perfect Judge?"*

defense.objection: "Evolution explains life. We don't need a Creator."
defense.response: Change in living things doesn't explain the first life, the information inside it, or the universe it lives in. And Scripture says God made everything in six days and made man directly, in His image. We are not the product of evolution. For the full case see [The fallacy of evolution](/topic/the-fallacy-of-evolution).
defense.askBack: *"Where did the first life, and the information in it, come from?"*

defense.objection: "Miracles are impossible."
defense.response: Only if there is no God, which assumes the answer. If God made the universe, raising a man is not hard for Him.
defense.askBack: *"If God created everything, is a resurrection too hard for Him?"*

defense.objection: "What about people who have never heard?"
defense.response: Everyone has creation and conscience, and everyone suppresses them. No one is condemned for not hearing, but for sin. The Judge of all the earth will do right. And you have heard.
defense.askBack: *"You've heard. What will you do with Jesus?"*

defense.objection: "Faith is believing without evidence."
defense.response: Biblical faith is trust in a Person on good grounds: eyewitness testimony and many convincing proofs.
defense.askBack: *"Do you trust anyone on the basis of testimony?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus never existed."
defense.response: Paul received the resurrection report within a few years and met Peter and James, the Lord's brother, in person.
defense.askBack: *"Who did Paul meet in Galatians 1:18–19?"*

intro.text: Winning the argument saves no one. Christ does. Say the whole message plainly, call for a response, and leave the results to God.

lines.label: God saves; you are faithful
lines.text: your job is to say the truth clearly. God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; Rom 1:16; John 6:44)

lines.label: Law before grace
lines.text: a person has to see their sin and God's judgment before the cross makes sense to them. (Rom 3:19–20; Gal 3:24)

lines.label: Jesus is Lord
lines.text: the call is to repent and follow Christ, not to repeat a prayer or add Jesus to a life that stays the same. (Luke 9:23; Rom 10:9; Acts 20:21)

lines.label: No false promises
lines.text: the gospel offers forgiveness and Christ Himself, not health, wealth or an easier life. (Phil 3:8; Mark 8:36; 2 Tim 3:12)
God created all things and made us for Himself. He is holy and just, He cannot overlook sin, and He will judge every person. (Gen 1:1; Isa 6:3; Hab 1:13; Acts 17:24–31; Heb 9:27)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What do you think happens after we die?"*

Every one of us has broken God's law. We are not basically good people who slip up; we are dead in sin, and the wages of sin is death. No amount of good works can pay it off. (Rom 3:10–12; Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Eph 2:1–3; Isa 64:6)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Have you kept God's law perfectly?"*

God the Son became man, lived the sinless life we have not lived, and died in the place of sinners, bearing the wrath they deserve. He was buried, rose bodily on the third day, and is Lord of all. (John 1:14; Isa 53:5–6; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 3:18; Rom 5:8; 1 Cor 15:3–4; Phil 2:9–11)
Only God can redeem a soul, and only a man can die in man's place, so the Savior is both. (Ps 49:7–9; Ps 49:15; 1 Tim 2:5–6; Heb 2:14–17)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Why did Jesus have to die?"*

God commands all people everywhere to repent. Whoever turns from sin and trusts in Christ alone is forgiven and has eternal life: by grace, through faith, not by works. Following Him costs everything, and no one who comes to Him is turned away. (Mark 1:15; Acts 17:30; John 3:16; Eph 2:8–9; Rom 10:9–13; Luke 14:27–28; John 6:37)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What is keeping you from turning to Christ today?"*

sections.heading: The short version: the Romans Road

lines.text: When you only have a minute, walk these in order, and call them to repent. (Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Rom 5:8; Acts 17:30; Rom 10:9–10; Rom 10:13; Rom 8:1)

sections.heading: How to walk someone through it

lines.text: For a step-by-step way to do this in a real conversation, using the Ten Commandments first and then the cross, open [The Way of the Master](/topic/the-way-of-the-master).

Pray with them. Get them a Bible and get them into a church that preaches it, where they can be baptized by immersion as a believer. Follow up. Don't pronounce them saved. Point them to Christ, and let assurance grow from following Him. (Acts 2:41–42; Matt 28:19–20; 2 Cor 13:5; 1 John 2:3–6; John 8:31)
Stay warm and leave the door open. You plant and water; God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; 1 Pet 3:15–16; 2 Tim 2:24–26)

topics.title: The Way of the Master

intro.text: God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble (James 4:6), so: law to the proud, grace to the humble. The Ten Commandments work like a mirror: they show a person their sin so that the cross makes sense. Jesus did this with the rich young ruler. (Rom 3:19–20; Rom 7:7; Gal 3:24; Mark 10:17–22)

lines.text: Move from ordinary talk to spiritual things with one question.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What do you think happens after we die?"*
Almost everyone says yes. Let them say it. (Prov 20:6)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Would you consider yourself a good person?"*

sections.heading: 3. Have you kept the Ten Commandments?

lines.text: Walk through a few, one at a time, and let them answer each. (Ex 20:1–17)

lines.label: Lying
lines.text: *"Have you ever told a lie? What does that make you?"*

lines.label: Stealing
lines.text: *"Have you ever taken anything that wasn't yours, whatever its value?"*

lines.label: God's name
lines.text: *"Have you ever used God's name as a curse word?"*

lines.label: Lust
lines.text: Jesus said that looking with lust is adultery in the heart. *"Have you ever done that?"* (Matt 5:27–28)

lines.label: Hatred
lines.text: Jesus put anger under the command "You shall not murder" (Matt 5:21–22), and John says whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15).
Sum up what they admitted in their own words, then ask. (Heb 9:27; Rom 2:15–16; James 2:10)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"If God judges you by that standard, will you be innocent or guilty?"*
Don't soften it, and don't gloat. Say it because you care where they end up. (Rev 21:8; 1 Cor 6:9–10)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Would that be heaven or hell? Does that concern you?"*
You stand guilty in God's courtroom, and Someone steps in and pays your fine in full. That is what Christ did on the cross, and He rose from the dead. (Rom 5:8; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 2:24; 1 Cor 15:3–4)
Believing a parachute exists won't save you; you have to put it on. Turn from sin and put your trust in Christ alone, today. (Acts 3:19; Acts 20:21; Rom 13:14; 2 Cor 6:2)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"When are you going to do that?"*
**Already humble?** If someone is broken over their sin, skip the law and go straight to grace.

lines.label: Aim at the conscience
lines.text: answering objections clears the path, but the law and the gospel do the work. Don't spend an hour on arguments and never get here. (Rom 2:15)

lines.label: Tone
lines.text: kind, patient, and plainly concerned for them. (2 Tim 2:24–26)
Then go back to [The Gospel](/topic/the-gospel) for the full message and what to do when they respond.

topics.subtitle: Use the law to reach the conscience, then give the gospel.

topics.title: Worldviews: how do you know?

intro.text: A presupposition is what a person takes for granted before the argument starts. The atheist is not neutral, and neither are you. He already knows God and suppresses that truth (Rom 1:18–21), so you are not handing him a God he has never met. You are showing him that he leans on God every time he reasons, judges or trusts his own mind. (Prov 1:7; Col 2:3; Ps 14:1; 1 Cor 1:20)

lines.text: You are not saying he knows nothing or believes in nothing. He reasons, does science and knows right from wrong, because he lives in God's world and is made in God's image. You are saying his worldview cannot **account for** any of it, and yours can. He is using the tools God gave him to argue against God.

lines.label: Say
lines.text: *"We both use reason. I'm not asking whether you reason. I'm asking why reason can be trusted if your view is true."*

sections.heading: Step 1: Don't give up your ground

lines.text: Do not agree to set the Bible aside and argue from "neutral" facts. No one is neutral, and Scripture is the standard, not the thing on trial. You start from what God has revealed. He starts from his own guess. (Prov 26:4; 2 Cor 10:5; 1 Pet 3:15)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Would you set aside your trust in reason to prove reason? Then why should I set aside God's word?"*

sections.heading: Step 2: Ask what he would accept

lines.text: Before you give evidence, find out what he counts as evidence. If he has no standard, he has no basis for saying there isn't any.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What would count as evidence for you?"*
**"Only what can be measured or tested."** → *"Did you measure that? Which experiment showed that only tested things are true?"* That rule is not something the five senses can find.
**"I don't know what would convince me."** → *"Then how do you know there's no evidence?"*
**"God is outside the universe, so He can't be tested."** → Evidence is more than lab results. We reason, weigh testimony and draw conclusions every day. (Acts 1:3; Heb 11:1)

sections.heading: Step 3: Step into his view and show it cannot stand

lines.text: Take his view on its own terms and ask what follows. One question at a time, and wait for the answer. (Prov 26:5)

lines.label: Knowledge
lines.text: *"How do you know that? How do you know anything for certain?"* If he says we can't know anything for certain: *"Are you certain of that?"*

lines.label: Logic
lines.text: *"Are the laws of logic made of matter? Do they change? Where do unchanging, universal laws come from in a universe of matter in motion?"* If he says God is illogical: *"That assumes logic is reliable. In your view, where does it come from?"*

lines.label: His own mind
lines.text: *"You said 'mind.' Is that anything more than brain chemistry? If your thoughts are chemistry shaped for survival, why trust them to tell you what is true?"*

lines.label: Science
lines.text: *"Why expect nature to act tomorrow the way it did today?"* (Gen 8:22; Col 1:17; Heb 1:3)

lines.label: Meaning
lines.text: *"If we came from nothing and go to nothing, on what basis does anything you do matter?"* If he says nothing has meaning: *"Does that sentence have meaning?"* (Eccl 1:2; Eccl 12:13–14)
Start here when he calls something evil, unfair or hateful.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Is morality objective, or is it opinion?"*

**"It's subjective."** → *"Then you can't say I'm wrong. You can only say you prefer something else, the way one person prefers burgers and another pizza."* Watch for him to keep saying you are wrong anyway. Point it out kindly.
**"It comes from my experience."** → *"Someone raised to hate his neighbors has experience too. Is his hatred good?"* Experience differs from person to person, so it cannot be the standard.
**"It comes from science."** → Science tells you what **is**. It cannot tell you what **ought** to be. *"Which experiment shows that lying is wrong?"*

**"That's just your interpretation of the Bible."** → Everyone interprets something: he interprets data and his own experience. Disagreement does not cancel truth. *"If someone says 1 + 1 = 3, does that make the answer uncertain?"*
**"That's true for you. This is my truth."** → An opinion is not the same as truth. Truth is what matches reality, whoever believes it. *"Can a person sincerely believe something and be wrong?"*
**"It's objective."** → *"Then who set the standard, and why does it bind everyone?"* (Rom 2:14–15)

Many people today have no Bible background. Words like sin, judgment and Savior mean little to someone who thinks he is an accident. Peter preached to people who knew the Scriptures and went straight to Christ and repentance (Acts 2:22–38). Paul, in Athens, began with the God who made the world and everything in it, and then said God now commands all people everywhere to repent (Acts 17:24–31). John's Gospel begins the same way: all things came into being through Christ (John 1:1–3; Col 1:16). You are not delaying the gospel. You are telling him whose world this is, so that sin makes sense and the cross is good news.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Who made you? And if you were made, who do you answer to?"*
**Made on purpose.** He is not a cosmic accident. He was made by God, in God's image, to know Him. (Gen 1:27; Ps 100:3; Ps 139:13–14)
